strategy_inputs.strategic_goals: Increase Revenue, Protect Revenue, Reduce Cost, Improve Customer Experience, Enable Data-Driven Decisions

use_cases.Name: Forecast Weekly Category Demand by Warehouse with Purchase Order Plan
use_cases.Statement: Buyers set purchase quantities without a forward view of combined catalog and web demand. Swings in `cs_quantity` and `ws_quantity` by `i_category` and warehouse leave some locations short and others carrying excess `inv_quantity_on_hand`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates `cs_quantity` and `ws_quantity` by `i_category`, `w_warehouse_sk` and `d_week_seq`. It fits seasonal forecasts with `d_holiday` and `d_moy` as regressors and nets the forecast against the latest `inv_quantity_on_hand`. The output is a ranked purchase order plan per category and warehouse.
use_cases.Business Value: The Merchandise Planner sets weekly buy quantities from forecast demand instead of trailing averages. This reduces the count of category-warehouse weeks where demand exceeds `inv_quantity_on_hand` and lowers excess on-hand units [ESTIMATE: depends on `inv_quantity_on_hand`].
use_cases.Tables Involved: samples.tpcds_sf1.catalog_sales, samples.tpcds_sf1.web_sales, samples.tpcds_sf1.inventory, samples.tpcds_sf1.item, samples.tpcds_sf1.date_dim, samples.tpcds_sf1.warehouse
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_sold_date_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_warehouse_sk, cs_quantity from catalog_sales; ws_sold_date_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_warehouse_sk, ws_quantity from web_sales; inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_date, d_week_seq, d_moy, d_holiday from date_dim; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse. Approach: (1) UNION ALL the catalog and web lines. (2) JOIN date_dim ON cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk (and ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk), and JOIN item ON cs_item_sk = i_item_sk (and ws_item_sk = i_item_sk). (3) Aggregate units per i_category x warehouse_sk x d_week_seq, with holiday_week = MAX(d_holiday = 'Y') and month = d_moy. (4) Fit Prophet per series with yearly seasonality, a holiday_week regressor and changepoint_prior_scale=0.05, validated by rolling-origin backtest MAPE. (5) JOIN the latest inventory snapshot ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk AND inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk, rolled up to category, and compute projected_gap = SUM(forecast_units over horizon) - on_hand. Output: i_category, w_warehouse_name, d_week_seq, forecast_units, lower, upper, on_hand, projected_gap, suggested_order_units. Final step: ai_query explains each series' seasonal and holiday drivers and drafts the buy recommendation per category-warehouse.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Cross-Warehouse Stock Transfers with Weekly Transfer Action List
use_cases.Statement: The same item can sit idle in one warehouse while selling through in another. Transfers ignore the gap between `inv_quantity_on_hand` and recent `cs_quantity` and `ws_quantity` velocity per `inv_warehouse_sk`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code computes weeks of cover per item and warehouse from `inv_quantity_on_hand` and trailing `cs_quantity` plus `ws_quantity`. It then solves a linear program that minimizes projected shortages, subject to safety-stock floors at source warehouses. The output is a weekly transfer action list.
use_cases.Business Value: The Inventory Control Manager moves units to where they are selling instead of reordering. This reduces item-warehouse weeks with projected shortage and lowers idle on-hand units valued at `i_wholesale_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on `inv_quantity_on_hand`].
use_cases.Tables Involved: samples.tpcds_sf1.inventory, samples.tpcds_sf1.catalog_sales, samples.tpcds_sf1.web_sales, samples.tpcds_sf1.warehouse, samples.tpcds_sf1.item, samples.tpcds_sf1.date_dim
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; cs_sold_date_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_warehouse_sk, cs_quantity from catalog_sales; ws_sold_date_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_warehouse_sk, ws_quantity from web_sales; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name, w_warehouse_sq_ft from warehouse; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_wholesale_cost from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) JOIN inventory to date_dim ON inv_date_sk = d_date_sk to get the latest d_week_seq snapshot. (2) Aggregate catalog and web units per item x warehouse x d_week_seq, joining ON cs_item_sk = inv_item_sk AND cs_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk (same pattern for web). (3) Compute velocity = trailing 8-week mean units, cover_weeks = on_hand / velocity and safety_stock = velocity x cover_floor_weeks. (4) Formulate an LP in OR-Tools: x(item, from, to) >= 0; shortage(item, to) >= velocity x horizon - on_hand_to - SUM(x into to); on_hand_from - SUM(x out of from) >= safety_stock_from; per-warehouse on-hand total <= historical max on-hand (capacity proxy alongside w_warehouse_sq_ft). (5) Objective: minimize SUM(shortage) + lambda x SUM(x), with lambda=0.1 as a transfer-effort penalty. Transfer cost data is not in the schema [MISSING_DATA: inter-warehouse transfer cost]. Output: i_item_id, from_warehouse, to_warehouse, transfer_units, shortage_units_avoided, source_cover_after. Final step: ai_query writes the rationale for each transfer and flags transfers the planner should confirm.

use_cases.Name: Segment Slow-Moving Inventory with Markdown and Clearance Candidate List
use_cases.Statement: Some item-warehouse positions hold high `inv_quantity_on_hand` while `cs_quantity` and `ws_quantity` sales stay flat. This ties up working capital valued at `i_wholesale_cost` with no clear markdown trigger.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds sell-through, cover, demand-volatility and margin-headroom features per item-warehouse from `inv_quantity_on_hand`, `cs_quantity`, `ws_quantity`, `i_current_price` and `i_wholesale_cost`. It clusters positions with K-Means to isolate slow movers. The output is a markdown and clearance candidate list.
use_cases.Business Value: The Markdown Analyst picks clearance items from a data-driven slow-mover cluster instead of age alone. This reduces on-hand wholesale value held in slow clusters (`inv_quantity_on_hand` x `i_wholesale_cost`) [ESTIMATE: depends on `inv_quantity_on_hand`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; cs_sold_date_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_warehouse_sk, cs_quantity from catalog_sales; ws_sold_date_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_warehouse_sk, ws_quantity from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_category, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) JOIN inventory and sales to date_dim ON inv_date_sk / cs_sold_date_sk / ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Aggregate per inv_item_sk x inv_warehouse_sk over the trailing window. (3) Engineer features: sell_through = units_sold / (units_sold + avg_on_hand); onhand_slope = OLS slope of weekly on_hand; demand_cv = stddev / mean of weekly units; weeks_since_last_sale; margin_headroom = (i_current_price - i_wholesale_cost) / i_current_price; held_value = avg_on_hand x i_wholesale_cost. (4) Standardize features and run K-Means with k chosen from 3 to 8 by silhouette (n_init=20). Label clusters by centroid profile (fast, steady, slow, dead). Output: i_item_id, warehouse_sk, cluster_label, sell_through, weeks_since_last_sale, held_value, max_markdown_depth = margin_headroom. Final step: ai_query explains each slow or dead cluster and recommends markdown depth versus liquidation per item within its headroom.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Weekly Web Demand by Category with Replenishment Plan
use_cases.Statement: Weekly units in `ws_quantity` for each `i_category` swing around `d_holiday` and `d_following_holiday` weeks. Without a forward view, replenishment for each `ws_warehouse_sk` is set from trailing totals, which leads to both overstock and lost `ws_ext_sales_price` in peak weeks.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates weekly `ws_quantity` and `ws_ext_sales_price` per `i_category` and `ws_warehouse_sk` on `d_week_seq`. It then fits a holiday-aware Prophet model per series. The output is a weekly replenishment plan per warehouse and category, with forecast ranges and recommended order-up adjustments.
use_cases.Business Value: The Demand Planner sets weekly replenishment quantities per warehouse and category from forecast ranges instead of trailing averages. This reduces forecast error on `ws_quantity` and recovers peak-week `ws_ext_sales_price` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_quantity`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_sold_date_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_warehouse_sk, ws_quantity, ws_ext_sales_price from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_date, d_week_seq, d_holiday, d_following_holiday from date_dim. Steps: (1) JOIN item ON web_sales.ws_item_sk = item.i_item_sk. (2) JOIN date_dim ON web_sales.ws_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk. (3) Aggregate weekly units and sales per i_category x ws_warehouse_sk. (4) Engineer a weekly holiday-count regressor from d_holiday and d_following_holiday. (5) Fit Prophet per series (yearly_seasonality on, changepoint_prior_scale=0.05). (6) Validate on a rolling 13-week holdout using MAPE. Output: i_category, ws_warehouse_sk, d_week_seq, yhat, yhat_lower, yhat_upper. [MISSING_DATA: on-hand inventory levels]. Final step: ai_query explains each forecast's drivers and recommends the replenishment adjustment per warehouse-category row.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Weekly Category Sales by Store with Purchase Planning Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: Category buyers set weekly purchase quantities without a forward view of `ss_quantity` and `ss_ext_sales_price` by store and `i_category`. As a result, weeks that contain `d_holiday` or `d_following_holiday` days are planned from last year's totals alone, which risks orders that are too large or too small.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates `ss_quantity` and `ss_ext_sales_price` by `s_store_name`, `i_category` and `d_week_seq`. It fits a Prophet model per series with weekly holiday counts from `d_holiday` as a regressor and backtests accuracy. It then publishes a 13-week store-by-category purchase planning list with forecast ranges for each buyer.
use_cases.Business Value: The Category Buyer sets weekly purchase quantities per store and category from forecast ranges instead of copying last year. This reduces backtested forecast error on `ss_quantity` and narrows the gap between planned and realized `ss_ext_sales_price` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_quantity`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_sold_date_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_quantity, ss_ext_sales_price from store_sales; d_date_sk, d_date, d_week_seq, d_year, d_holiday, d_following_holiday from date_dim; i_item_sk, i_category from item; s_store_sk, s_store_name from store. Joins: store_sales to date_dim ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk; to item ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk; to store ON ss_store_sk = s_store_sk. Aggregate weekly units and sales per (s_store_name, i_category, d_week_seq). Engineer holiday_days = COUNT of days with d_holiday = 'Y' in the week, and a post-holiday flag from d_following_holiday. Fit Prophet per series with yearly seasonality and changepoint_prior_scale=0.05, using holiday_days as an extra regressor. Backtest with rolling-origin validation over the last 26 weeks and report MAPE. Output: s_store_name, i_category, d_week_seq, forecast_units, lower_80, upper_80, forecast_sales, backtest_mape. ai_query receives the largest forecast-versus-last-year deviations and writes purchase-quantity recommendations per category for the buyer.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Weekly Category Demand with Replenishment Planning Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: Merchandise planners set purchase volumes without a forward view of weekly units sold (`cs_quantity`) and revenue (`cs_ext_sales_price`) by `i_category` and `i_class`. Holiday weeks flagged in `d_holiday` therefore risk both stockouts and overbuying.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins catalog sales to item and date, aggregates weekly `cs_quantity` and `cs_ext_sales_price` by `i_category` and `i_class` over `d_week_seq`, and fits a Prophet model with holiday and weekend regressors from `d_holiday` and `d_weekend`. The final output is a weekly category replenishment plan listing forecast units with upper and lower bounds.
use_cases.Business Value: The Merchandise Planner sets class-level buy quantities each week from the forecast bands, with the goal of reducing forecast error on weekly `cs_quantity` and lowering unsold buys [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_quantity`]. Forecast accuracy (MAPE on `cs_quantity`) is tracked weekly against actuals.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_sold_date_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_quantity, cs_ext_sales_price from catalog_sales; i_item_sk, i_category, i_class from item; d_date_sk, d_date, d_week_seq, d_holiday, d_weekend from date_dim. Join: catalog_sales JOIN item ON cs_item_sk = i_item_sk JOIN date_dim ON cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Aggregate weekly units and revenue per i_category and i_class. Build regressors: holiday_days = count of d_holiday = 'Y' in the week; weekend_share = share of units sold where d_weekend = 'Y'. Fit Prophet per series with yearly seasonality and changepoint_prior_scale=0.05, then backtest MAPE on the last 13 weeks. Output schema: (i_category, i_class, d_week_seq, forecast_units, lower_80, upper_80, forecast_revenue). [MISSING_DATA: on-hand inventory] is needed to convert the forecast into order quantities. As a final step, ai_query explains the drivers of each forecast and recommends purchase-volume adjustments per class.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Category Stock Levels by Warehouse with Replenishment Planning Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: Planners have no forward view of `inv_quantity_on_hand` by `i_category` and `w_warehouse_name`, so replenishment is set on past snapshots. Each category in each warehouse risks running short or carrying excess stock in the coming weeks.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `inventory` to `item`, `warehouse` and `date_dim`, aggregates `inv_quantity_on_hand` by `d_week_seq`, `i_category` and `w_warehouse_name`, and fits a seasonal time-series forecast with holiday-week regressors from `d_holiday`. The output is a weekly replenishment planning recommendation list that flags each category-warehouse pair projected to fall below its own historical lower band.
use_cases.Business Value: The Inventory Planner sets replenishment orders from projected stock instead of the last snapshot. The target is to reduce the count of category-warehouse weeks where `inv_quantity_on_hand` reaches zero [ESTIMATE: depends on inv_quantity_on_hand] and to reduce forecast error on `inv_quantity_on_hand` against actuals.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_category from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_date, d_week_seq, d_holiday from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join inventory to item ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, to warehouse ON inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk, and to date_dim ON inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Aggregate SUM(inv_quantity_on_hand) per d_week_seq, i_category and w_warehouse_name. (3) Derive a holiday_week flag, equal to 1 when any d_date in the week has d_holiday = 'Y'. (4) Fit Prophet per series with yearly seasonality, holiday_week as an extra regressor and changepoint_prior_scale = 0.05, over a 13-week horizon. Backtest with rolling-origin MAPE. (5) Output columns: category, warehouse, week, yhat, yhat_lower, yhat_upper and below_band_flag. (6) ai_query receives each flagged series with its forecast and recent history and writes a plain-language replenishment recommendation per category-warehouse.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Launch Stock Depth for New Item Records with Initial Allocation Guidelines
use_cases.Statement: New item records, identified by `i_rec_start_date`, are stocked without evidence of how earlier cohorts' `inv_quantity_on_hand` evolved in the weeks after introduction. This leads either to early zero stock or to lingering excess.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code groups items into cohorts by the quarter of `i_rec_start_date` and `i_category`. It then tracks each cohort's average `inv_quantity_on_hand` and zero-stock share by weeks since record start, using `d_date`. The output is an initial allocation guideline per category for new item records.
use_cases.Business Value: The New Product Planner sets opening stock depth for new item records from cohort evidence instead of flat defaults. The targets are to reduce early-life zero-stock share and to reduce excess capital computed from `inv_quantity_on_hand` and `i_wholesale_cost` in the first weeks [ESTIMATE: depends on inv_quantity_on_hand].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_rec_start_date, i_category, i_wholesale_cost from item; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) cohort = quarter of i_rec_start_date crossed with i_category. (3) weeks_since_start = FLOOR(DATEDIFF(d_date, i_rec_start_date) / 7). Keep rows where weeks_since_start >= 0. (4) Per cohort and weeks_since_start, compute mean qty, zero_share (inv_quantity_on_hand = 0) and mean capital = qty * i_wholesale_cost. (5) Build a cohort retention-style matrix and compare the cohort curves with a Kruskal-Wallis test. (6) Output columns: i_category, weeks_since_start, median_qty_curve, zero_share_curve and recommended_opening_depth (the percentile of early-week qty that kept zero_share lowest). (7) ai_query writes an allocation guideline for each category. Note: i_rec_start_date may mark a record version rather than a true launch.

use_cases.Name: Detect Unexplained Stock Swings by Item and Warehouse with Investigation Queue
use_cases.Statement: Sudden, unexplained changes in `inv_quantity_on_hand` for an `inv_item_sk` at one `inv_warehouse_sk` may signal record errors or unrecorded losses. Today these go uninvestigated, and their value at `i_wholesale_cost` is never measured.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds snapshot-over-snapshot change features per item-warehouse from `inv_quantity_on_hand` and `inv_date_sk`. Each change is valued at `i_wholesale_cost` and compared with the same item in other warehouses, then an Isolation Forest scores the changes. The output is a cost-ranked investigation queue for warehouse control teams.
use_cases.Business Value: The Loss Prevention Manager sends cycle counts to the item-warehouse pairs with the highest anomaly scores and the largest swings valued at cost. The target is to reduce the unexplained change in `inv_quantity_on_hand` valued at `i_wholesale_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on i_wholesale_cost] and to increase the share of counts that confirm a discrepancy.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_wholesale_cost, i_category from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Order each item-warehouse series by d_week_seq. (3) Engineer features: delta_qty = inv_quantity_on_hand minus LAG(inv_quantity_on_hand); delta_pct = delta_qty / NULLIF(LAG qty, 0); delta_value = delta_qty * i_wholesale_cost; peer_gap = delta_qty minus the median delta_qty of the same inv_item_sk across the other warehouses in the same d_week_seq; vol_8 = the rolling 8-snapshot STDDEV of delta_qty; z_local = delta_qty / vol_8. (4) Train an Isolation Forest with contamination = 0.01 and n_estimators = 200 on these features. (5) Output columns: inv_item_sk, w_warehouse_name, d_week_seq, delta_qty, delta_value, anomaly_score and rank. (6) ai_query explains why each top-ranked swing is unusual compared with its peers and history, and recommends a count-or-review action.

use_cases.Name: Prioritize Inventory Capital Reduction by Merchandise Manager with Buy-Down Target List
use_cases.Statement: Inventory capital, defined as `inv_quantity_on_hand` times `i_wholesale_cost`, is likely concentrated in a small set of brands within each `i_manager_id` portfolio. Without knowing which brands persistently dominate, buy-down effort is spread thinly across items.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code values every snapshot at cost and builds cumulative Pareto curves of capital by `i_brand` within each `i_manager_id`. It then scores each brand's persistence, meaning how many `d_quarter_seq` periods it stays in the top contributor set. The output is a buy-down target list per manager.
use_cases.Business Value: The Merchandise Manager focuses purchase reductions on the brands that persistently hold the most capital. The targets are to reduce total inventory capital at cost computed from `inv_quantity_on_hand` and `i_wholesale_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on i_wholesale_cost] and to increase the capital freed per brand addressed.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_wholesale_cost, i_brand, i_manager_id, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_quarter_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) capital = inv_quantity_on_hand * i_wholesale_cost. (3) Average capital per i_brand and i_manager_id within each d_quarter_seq. (4) Rank brands within each manager and compute the cumulative capital share. Flag the brands that make up the first 80 percent of capital. (5) persistence = COUNT of quarters flagged / total quarters. Keep the brands where both persistence and capital share are high. (6) Output columns: i_manager_id, i_brand, i_category, avg_capital, cum_share, persistence and priority_rank. (7) ai_query writes a buy-down rationale and a suggested review sequence for each manager.

use_cases.Name: Segment Items by Stock Behavior with Differentiated Stocking Policies
use_cases.Statement: Every item is managed with the same stocking approach, even though the history of `inv_quantity_on_hand` shows very different volatility, zero-stock frequency and capital at `i_wholesale_cost`. As a result, stable items are overstocked and volatile items run short.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers behavior features per item and warehouse from `inv_quantity_on_hand` over `d_week_seq`, enriched with `i_current_price` and `i_wholesale_cost`, and groups them with K-Means. The output is a stocking policy assignment table that maps each item-warehouse to a cluster-specific policy.
use_cases.Business Value: The Replenishment Manager applies a different review frequency and stock floor to each cluster instead of one rule for all items. The targets are to reduce average capital at cost in the stable clusters [ESTIMATE: depends on i_wholesale_cost] and to reduce the zero-stock share computed from `inv_quantity_on_hand` in the volatile clusters.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) For each item-warehouse pair, compute: mean_qty, cv_qty = STDDEV / mean, slope_qty from a linear fit of qty on d_week_seq, zero_share = share of snapshots with inv_quantity_on_hand = 0, avg_capital = mean_qty * i_wholesale_cost, and unit_margin = i_current_price minus i_wholesale_cost. (3) Standardize the features and run K-Means with k selected from 4 to 8 by silhouette score. (4) Output columns: inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, cluster_id and the cluster centroid profile. (5) ai_query reads each centroid profile and proposes a named stocking policy (review cadence, floor logic, buy-down or protect) for that cluster.

use_cases.Name: Predict Next-Period Stockouts by Item and Warehouse with Expedite Priority Queue
use_cases.Statement: Item-warehouse pairs whose `inv_quantity_on_hand` will hit zero at the next snapshot are found only after the fact. This leaves no time to expedite supply for items with a high `i_current_price`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code trains an XGBoost classifier on lagged `inv_quantity_on_hand` features, item attributes such as `i_category` and `i_current_price`, and calendar context from `d_moy` and `d_holiday`. The model predicts whether each item-warehouse will have zero stock at the next snapshot. The output is an expedite priority queue ranked by stockout probability times `i_current_price`.
use_cases.Business Value: The Replenishment Manager expedites the top of the queue each cycle, ahead of the stockout. The targets are to reduce the count of next-snapshot zero `inv_quantity_on_hand` events [ESTIMATE: depends on inv_quantity_on_hand] and to increase the precision of expedite actions measured against realized zero-stock events.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_category, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_moy, d_holiday from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Label = 1 if LEAD(inv_quantity_on_hand) = 0, ordered by d_week_seq. (3) Features: lag1 to lag4 qty, the 4- and 8-snapshot rolling mean and slope, min_qty_8, historical zero_share, i_category one-hot, i_current_price, d_moy of the next snapshot, and a next-week holiday flag from d_holiday. (4) Train XGBoost with max_depth = 6, eta = 0.1 and scale_pos_weight set from the class ratio, using a time-based train/test split by d_week_seq. Evaluate with PR-AUC and log the run in MLflow. Compute SHAP values for each row. (5) Output columns: inv_item_sk, w_warehouse_name, p_stockout, revenue_at_risk_proxy = p_stockout * i_current_price, top_shap_drivers and rank. (6) ai_query turns the top SHAP drivers of each queued item into an expedite recommendation.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Pre-Holiday Stock Build by Category with Pre-Season Build Plan
use_cases.Statement: Holiday periods flagged by `d_holiday` and `d_following_holiday` may deplete category stock in `inv_quantity_on_hand` unevenly. Without measuring how much each `i_category` draws down around holidays, pre-season builds are sized by habit.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code fits a Ridge regression per category of weekly stock on holiday, post-holiday and month indicators drawn from `d_holiday`, `d_following_holiday` and `d_moy`. It isolates the holiday drawdown effect for each category. The output is a pre-season build plan that ranks the categories needing a larger build.
use_cases.Business Value: The Seasonal Planner raises pre-holiday builds for the categories with significant post-holiday drawdown and holds builds flat elsewhere. The targets are to reduce post-holiday zero-stock events in `inv_quantity_on_hand` [ESTIMATE: depends on inv_quantity_on_hand] and to reduce excess stock carried after holiday weeks.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_moy, d_year, d_holiday, d_following_holiday from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Aggregate SUM(inv_quantity_on_hand) per i_category and d_week_seq. (3) Build week-level flags: holiday_week (any d_holiday = 'Y'), post_holiday_week (any d_following_holiday = 'Y'), d_moy dummies and a linear trend on d_week_seq. (4) Fit Ridge regression with alpha = 1.0 on log(stock) per category. Use bootstrap confidence intervals for the holiday_week and post_holiday_week coefficients. (5) Output columns: i_category, holiday_effect, post_holiday_effect, ci_low, ci_high and build_priority. (6) ai_query turns each category's coefficients into a pre-season build recommendation, with stated confidence.

use_cases.Name: Detect Structural Shifts in Category Stock Holdings with Purchasing Adjustment Alerts
use_cases.Statement: Gradual, lasting shifts in capital at cost (`inv_quantity_on_hand` times `i_wholesale_cost`) by `i_category` and `w_warehouse_name` hide beneath seasonal noise. Purchasing reacts only after bloat or depletion is entrenched.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code decomposes each category-warehouse capital series over `d_week_seq` with STL, then runs change-point detection on the trend component to find lasting level shifts. The output is a purchasing adjustment alert list naming each shifted series, the shift date and its direction.
use_cases.Business Value: The Purchasing Manager cuts or raises open buys for categories as soon as a lasting shift is confirmed. The targets are to reduce the number of weeks capital stays above its pre-shift level [ESTIMATE: depends on i_wholesale_cost] and to reduce depletion periods in `inv_quantity_on_hand`.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_category, i_wholesale_cost from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) capital = SUM(inv_quantity_on_hand * i_wholesale_cost) per i_category, w_warehouse_name and d_week_seq. (3) Apply STL decomposition with period = 52 and robust = true. (4) Run the PELT change-point algorithm (ruptures library) with an RBF cost on the trend component. Set the penalty by a BIC-style rule. (5) Output columns: category, warehouse, change_week, pre_level, post_level, direction and persistence_weeks. (6) ai_query writes an alert explaining each shift and the recommended purchasing adjustment.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Safety Stock Targets by Item and Warehouse with Reorder Point Settings
use_cases.Statement: Buffer levels for each `inv_item_sk` and `inv_warehouse_sk` pair are not tied to the observed week-to-week variability of `inv_quantity_on_hand`. As a result, some pairs carry excess units valued at `i_wholesale_cost` while others repeatedly fall to zero.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code derives net weekly drawdown from consecutive `inv_quantity_on_hand` snapshots ordered by `d_week_seq`, estimates drawdown mean and variability per item and warehouse, and solves a service-constrained optimization that minimizes buffer value at `i_wholesale_cost` within each `i_category`. The output is a reorder point settings table per item and warehouse for the planning system.
use_cases.Business Value: The Inventory Planner resets reorder points per item and warehouse each month. The target is fewer stockout weeks (snapshots where `inv_quantity_on_hand` equals zero) and lower buffer value at `i_wholesale_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on `inv_quantity_on_hand`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim; i_item_sk, i_wholesale_cost, i_category from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse. Join on inventory.inv_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk, inventory.inv_item_sk = item.i_item_sk and inventory.inv_warehouse_sk = warehouse.w_warehouse_sk. Feature engineering: drawdown = LAG(inv_quantity_on_hand) minus inv_quantity_on_hand, partitioned by item and warehouse and ordered by d_week_seq, keeping positive values only; drawdown_mu and drawdown_sigma over a trailing 26-week window; stockout_flag = inv_quantity_on_hand = 0. Optimization: a PuLP linear program minimizes the sum of safety_stock_units times i_wholesale_cost, subject to safety_stock_units >= z_category times drawdown_sigma, where z_category comes from a planner-set service grid per i_category, and subject to a category buffer-value cap. Output: inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, safety_stock_units, reorder_point_units = drawdown_mu plus safety_stock_units, buffer_value. ai_query then receives each change against current average on-hand and writes a one-line justification for the planner.

use_cases.Name: Recommend Joint Replenishment Groups for Co-Depleting Items with Consolidated Order Plan
use_cases.Statement: Items from the same `i_manufact_id` whose `inv_quantity_on_hand` draws down in the same weeks at the same `inv_warehouse_sk` are replenished independently. This multiplies separate replenishment events per manufacturer and warehouse.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds an item-to-item graph per warehouse. Edges are weighted by the correlation of weekly drawdown series over `d_week_seq` and restricted to items sharing `i_manufact_id`. Community detection then finds co-depleting groups, and the output is a consolidated order plan listing each item group, its manufacturer, warehouse and shared order week.
use_cases.Business Value: The Procurement Buyer places one order per co-depleting group instead of one per item. The goal is to reduce the count of separate replenishment events (positive jumps in `inv_quantity_on_hand`) per `i_manufact_id` and warehouse [ESTIMATE: depends on `inv_quantity_on_hand`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim; i_item_sk, i_manufact_id, i_manufact, i_category from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse. Join on inv_date_sk = d_date_sk, inv_item_sk = i_item_sk and inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk. Feature engineering: weekly drawdown series per item and warehouse = positive part of LAG(inv_quantity_on_hand) minus inv_quantity_on_hand; receipt_event = negative delta. Build GraphFrames edges between items with the same i_manufact_id and warehouse where the Spearman correlation of the drawdown series is >= 0.6 over at least 26 shared weeks; edge weight = correlation. Run Louvain community detection (networkx, resolution = 1.0) per warehouse; compute current receipt_event count per community versus a single shared cadence. Output: community_id, w_warehouse_name, i_manufact, item list, proposed order week of cycle, current_receipt_events. ai_query then explains each group's co-depletion evidence and drafts the consolidated order instruction for the buyer.

use_cases.Name: Predict Stock Run-Off Time for Superseded Item Versions with Liquidation Priority List
use_cases.Statement: Item versions whose `i_rec_end_date` has passed still hold `inv_quantity_on_hand` in warehouses. Without an estimate of how long that stock takes to run off, units valued at `i_wholesale_cost` sit unmanaged.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code treats `i_rec_end_date` as the start event and the first snapshot where `inv_quantity_on_hand` reaches zero at a warehouse as the end event, with right-censoring when stock remains. A Cox proportional hazards model is fit on price, cost, category and warehouse covariates. The output is a liquidation priority list ranking superseded item-warehouse pairs by predicted run-off time times stock value.
use_cases.Business Value: The Clearance Manager liquidates the slowest-predicted superseded stock first. The goal is to reduce the value of `inv_quantity_on_hand` times `i_wholesale_cost` held on item versions past `i_rec_end_date` [ESTIMATE: depends on `i_wholesale_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_rec_end_date, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost, i_category, i_class from item; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse. Join on inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_date_sk = d_date_sk and inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk; keep rows where i_rec_end_date is not null and d_date >= i_rec_end_date. Feature engineering: duration = days from i_rec_end_date to the first d_date with inv_quantity_on_hand = 0, with event_observed = 1, otherwise censored at the last snapshot; covariates are qty_at_end (on-hand at the first snapshot after i_rec_end_date), margin = i_current_price minus i_wholesale_cost, i_category, w_warehouse_name, and whether the same i_item_id has a newer active version. Fit Kaplan-Meier curves by category for baseline and lifelines CoxPHFitter (penalizer = 0.1) for individual predictions. Output: inv_item_sk, i_item_id, w_warehouse_name, predicted_median_runoff_days, stranded_value = remaining qty times i_wholesale_cost, priority_rank. ai_query then explains the hazard drivers for each pair and recommends liquidation actions.

use_cases.Name: Detect Low-Margin Items Stocked Beyond Peer Norms with Purchase Cut Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: Some items with thin unit margin (`i_current_price` minus `i_wholesale_cost`) carry average `inv_quantity_on_hand` far above comparable items in the same `i_class` and warehouse. This ties capital to the least profitable stock.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code fits a Ridge regression of log average on-hand on margin, cost, class, brand, warehouse and observed drawdown rate to estimate the expected stock depth for each item. Large positive residuals on low-margin items are then ranked to produce a purchase cut recommendation list per buyer.
use_cases.Business Value: The Category Buyer reduces future purchase quantities on low-margin items stocked above peer norms. The KPI is a decrease in excess units (actual minus expected `inv_quantity_on_hand`) and in excess value at `i_wholesale_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on `i_wholesale_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost, i_class_id, i_class, i_brand_id, i_category, i_manager_id from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Join on inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. Feature engineering per item and warehouse over the trailing 52 weeks: avg_on_hand, log_avg_on_hand = LN(1 + avg_on_hand), unit_margin = i_current_price minus i_wholesale_cost, margin_pct = unit_margin / i_current_price, drawdown_rate = mean positive weekly decrease in inv_quantity_on_hand, plus one-hot i_class_id and warehouse. Fit Ridge regression (alpha = 1.0, 5-fold cross-validation) on log_avg_on_hand. Compute residual = actual minus predicted, and flag items in the bottom margin_pct quartile within i_category with standardized residual > 2. Output: inv_item_sk, w_warehouse_name, i_manager_id, expected_units, excess_units, excess_value = excess_units times i_wholesale_cost. ai_query then explains each item's main drivers and recommends a purchase cut quantity.

use_cases.Name: Prioritize Cycle Counts by Item and Warehouse with Weekly Count Schedule
use_cases.Statement: Snapshots where `inv_quantity_on_hand` is NULL or shows implausible jumps leave some `inv_item_sk` and `inv_warehouse_sk` records unreliable. Counting effort is not directed to the pairs most likely to have the next bad reading.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code labels each item-warehouse-week by whether the next snapshot is missing or implausible, then trains an XGBoost classifier on reading history, volatility, value and category. The output is a weekly count schedule that ranks pairs by predicted inaccuracy probability times stock value at `i_wholesale_cost`.
use_cases.Business Value: The Inventory Control Manager assigns counters from the weekly schedule. The goal is to reduce the number of NULL or implausible `inv_quantity_on_hand` readings on high-value item-warehouse pairs [ESTIMATE: depends on `inv_quantity_on_hand`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_wholesale_cost, i_category, i_class from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Join on inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. Label: next_week_bad = 1 if the next d_week_seq reading is NULL, or if its absolute delta exceeds the pair's rolling P99 absolute delta. Features: null_count_prior_26w, weeks_since_last_null, delta_cv_26w, max_abs_delta_26w, avg_on_hand, stock_value = avg_on_hand times i_wholesale_cost, i_category, i_class, w_warehouse_name. Train XGBoost (max_depth = 6, eta = 0.1, scale_pos_weight set to the class-imbalance ratio) with a time-based split on d_week_seq, and report SHAP values for explainability. Output: inv_item_sk, w_warehouse_name, bad_reading_probability, count_priority = probability times stock_value, scheduled_count_week. ai_query then explains the top SHAP drivers for each scheduled pair in plain language for counters.

use_cases.Name: Predict Customer Repurchase Timing with Win-Back Outreach Schedule
use_cases.Statement: Outreach is sent on fixed calendars, so it is not tied to each customer's likely next purchase window. The time between purchases in `ss_sold_date_sk`, `ws_sold_date_sk` and `cs_sold_date_sk` varies with frequency, return behavior and `c_preferred_cust_flag`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds inter-purchase spells per customer with censoring at the data end. It fits a Cox proportional hazards model on frequency, spend, channel mix, return rate and `c_preferred_cust_flag`, and estimates when each customer's repurchase probability drops. The output is a dated win-back outreach schedule.
use_cases.Business Value: The Retention Marketing Manager times win-back contact to each customer's predicted lapse point instead of a fixed calendar. This reduces the share of customers passing their predicted window without a purchase and protects repeat `ss_net_paid` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_net_paid`].
use_cases.Tables Involved: samples.tpcds_sf1.store_sales, samples.tpcds_sf1.web_sales, samples.tpcds_sf1.catalog_sales, samples.tpcds_sf1.store_returns, samples.tpcds_sf1.customer, samples.tpcds_sf1.date_dim
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_customer_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_ticket_number, ss_net_paid from store_sales; ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_order_number, ws_net_paid from web_sales; cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_order_number, cs_net_paid from catalog_sales; sr_customer_sk, sr_return_quantity from store_returns; c_customer_sk, c_customer_id, c_preferred_cust_flag from customer; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim. Approach: (1) UNION orders across channels at order grain (distinct ticket/order number) and JOIN date_dim ON sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) For each order, duration = days to the customer's next order, with event = 1 if a next order exists, else censored at max d_date. (3) Time-varying covariates at order time: prior_order_count, avg_net_paid, web_share, catalog_share, prior return count from store_returns (JOIN ON sr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk), and c_preferred_cust_flag. (4) Fit lifelines CoxPHFitter (penalizer=0.1), check proportional hazards with Schoenfeld residuals, and plot Kaplan-Meier curves by frequency band. (5) For each customer's latest order, predict the survival curve; lapse_date = date when P(no repurchase yet) crosses the selected threshold. Output: c_customer_id, last_order_date, median_days_to_next, lapse_date, hazard_ratio_drivers. Final step: ai_query writes each customer's win-back reason and recommended outreach date and channel.

use_cases.Name: Classify Customers Likely to Qualify as Preferred with Enrollment Target List
use_cases.Statement: Many customers with `c_preferred_cust_flag` = N buy in ways similar to preferred customers in `ss_net_paid` and `ws_net_paid`. The business has no ranked list of whom to invite.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code trains an XGBoost classifier on purchase frequency, spend, channel mix and return behavior, using customers whose `c_preferred_cust_flag` is Y or N as labels. It scores non-preferred customers by preferred-likeness. The output is an enrollment target list.
use_cases.Business Value: The Loyalty Program Manager invites the highest-scoring non-preferred customers. This increases the count of customers with `c_preferred_cust_flag` = Y and net paid per enrolled customer versus a holdout [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_net_paid`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: c_customer_sk, c_customer_id, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year from customer; ss_customer_sk, ss_ticket_number, ss_net_paid, ss_sold_date_sk from store_sales; ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_order_number, ws_net_paid from web_sales; cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_order_number, cs_net_paid from catalog_sales; sr_customer_sk, sr_return_amt from store_returns. Approach: (1) Aggregate each channel per customer and JOIN to customer ON ss_customer_sk / ws_bill_customer_sk / cs_bill_customer_sk / sr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk. (2) Features: order_count per channel, total_net_paid, avg_ticket_value, channel_count, recency, return_rate = SUM(sr_return_amt) / store net paid, and age derived from c_birth_year. (3) Label = c_preferred_cust_flag = 'Y'; drop nulls. (4) Train XGBoost (max_depth=5, eta=0.1, n_estimators=300) with 5-fold CV ROC-AUC. If AUC is near random, the flag is not behavior-driven and the UC should stop. Apply SHAP for explanations. (5) Score N customers. Output: c_customer_id, propensity, total_net_paid, top_shap_features, decile. Final step: ai_query writes an invitation rationale and recommended offer per top-decile customer.

use_cases.Name: Identify Weak Customer Acquisition Cohorts with Reactivation Campaign Plan
use_cases.Statement: Customers acquired in different months and through different first channels may decay at very different rates in repeat `ss_net_paid`, `cs_net_paid` and `ws_net_paid`. Reactivation spend is not directed at the cohorts that fall off fastest.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code forms cohorts by first purchase month and first channel, cross-checked against `c_first_sales_date_sk`. It builds retention and cumulative `ss_net_paid` / `ws_net_paid` / `cs_net_paid` curves by months since acquisition. The output is a reactivation campaign plan listing lapsed customers in under-performing cohorts.
use_cases.Business Value: The CRM Manager targets reactivation at cohorts whose month-k retention trails the cohort median. This increases repeat-purchase rate and cumulative net paid per acquired customer [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_net_paid`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_customer_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_net_paid from store_sales; ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_net_paid from web_sales; cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_net_paid from catalog_sales; c_customer_sk, c_customer_id, c_first_sales_date_sk from customer; d_date_sk, d_month_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) UNION the three channels into customer_sk, date_sk, net_paid and channel. (2) JOIN date_dim ON date_sk = d_date_sk and JOIN customer ON customer_sk = c_customer_sk. (3) cohort_month = MIN(d_month_seq) per customer; first_channel = channel at that month. Validate against c_first_sales_date_sk mapped through date_dim. (4) Build a matrix of active_share and cumulative net_paid per cohort_month x first_channel x months_since. (5) Flag cohorts below the median curve at months_since 3, 6 and 12. List customers in flagged cohorts with no purchase in the last 3 months, ranked by prior net_paid. Output: cohort_month, first_channel, months_since, active_share, cum_net_paid, flag; plus c_customer_id, last_purchase_month, prior_net_paid. Final step: ai_query explains why each flagged cohort decays (channel, timing) and proposes campaign messaging per cohort.

use_cases.Name: Predict Repeat Web Buyer Lapse with Retention Outreach Queue
use_cases.Statement: Repeat web buyers stop ordering without warning. The gap only shows up after the fact, as a falling count of `ws_order_number` per `ws_bill_customer_sk` and lost `ws_net_paid`. Retention teams therefore react too late to save the customer.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds recency, frequency, monetary, discount and tenure features per customer from `ws_net_paid`, `ws_ext_discount_amt`, `ws_coupon_amt` and `c_first_sales_date_sk`. It trains an XGBoost lapse classifier on these features. The output is a weekly retention outreach queue ranked by lapse probability multiplied by expected `ws_net_paid` at risk.
use_cases.Business Value: The Customer Retention Manager targets outreach at the customers with the highest value at risk instead of using blanket campaigns. This reduces the lapse rate measured on `ws_order_number` per customer and protects `ws_net_paid` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_net_paid`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_order_number, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_net_paid, ws_ext_discount_amt, ws_ext_list_price, ws_coupon_amt from web_sales; c_customer_sk, c_first_sales_date_sk, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year from customer; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim. Joins: web_sales JOIN customer ON ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk; JOIN date_dim ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk; a second date_dim join ON c_first_sales_date_sk = d_date_sk gives tenure. Features at each monthly snapshot: (a) days since last d_date; (b) distinct ws_order_number in trailing 180 days; (c) sum ws_net_paid; (d) discount depth = sum ws_ext_discount_amt / sum ws_ext_list_price; (e) coupon order share; (f) tenure days; (g) c_preferred_cust_flag; (h) age from c_birth_year. Label: no order in the next 90 days. Model: XGBoost (max_depth=6, eta=0.1, n_estimators=400) with a time-based train/test split, evaluated on AUC, with SHAP explanations. Output: c_customer_sk, lapse_probability, value_at_risk, top_3_drivers. Final step: ai_query writes a per-customer outreach rationale and suggested contact angle.

use_cases.Name: Predict Time to Second Web Purchase with New Buyer Nurture Schedule
use_cases.Statement: Many first-time buyers, identified by their first `ws_sold_date_sk` per `ws_bill_customer_sk`, never place a second `ws_order_number`. Nurture messages are sent on a fixed calendar that ignores how quickly each type of first order normally converts to a repeat purchase.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds time-to-second-order data, with censoring, from `ws_order_number` dates per customer. It fits Kaplan-Meier curves by first-order `i_category` and a Cox model using first-order `ws_net_paid`, `ws_coupon_amt` and `c_preferred_cust_flag`. The output is a per-customer nurture schedule timed just before each customer's predicted drop-off point.
use_cases.Business Value: The Customer Lifecycle Manager times nurture touches per new buyer from their predicted hazard instead of a fixed calendar. This increases the second-order rate measured on `ws_order_number` and shortens time to second purchase [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_order_number`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_order_number, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_net_paid, ws_coupon_amt, ws_ext_discount_amt, ws_ext_list_price from web_sales; c_customer_sk, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year from customer; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim; i_item_sk, i_category from item. Joins: JOIN date_dim ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk; JOIN customer ON ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk; JOIN item ON ws_item_sk = i_item_sk. Per customer: start = MIN(d_date) of the first ws_order_number; event = d_date of the second distinct ws_order_number; customers without a second order are censored at the max d_date in the data. First-order covariates: total ws_net_paid, coupon flag (ws_coupon_amt > 0), discount depth, dominant i_category, c_preferred_cust_flag, age from c_birth_year. Fit Kaplan-Meier curves by first-order i_category (lifelines), then a Cox PH model (penalizer=0.1), checking the proportional-hazards assumption with Schoenfeld residuals. Output: c_customer_sk, predicted median days to second order, hazard ratio, recommended nurture day. Final step: ai_query writes the nurture message angle per customer group.

use_cases.Name: Identify Low-Value Acquisition Cohorts by Store with Store Acquisition Action Plan
use_cases.Statement: Stores acquire new shoppers every month (the first-ticket month is MIN `d_month_seq` per `ss_customer_sk`). Whether those cohorts deliver sustained `ss_net_profit` over the following 12 months differs by first store and first-basket discount depth, and this is not tracked.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds acquisition cohorts by first month, first `s_store_name` and first-basket discount tercile from `ss_ext_discount_amt` and `ss_coupon_amt`. It tracks cumulative `ss_net_profit` per shopper over 12 months since acquisition, with bootstrapped confidence intervals, and delivers a store acquisition action plan that flags acquisition contexts producing low-value cohorts.
use_cases.Business Value: The Customer Insights Manager advises store managers to stop deep first-visit discounting where those cohorts underperform. This increases 12-month cumulative `ss_net_profit` per newly acquired shopper [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_net_profit`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_customer_sk, ss_ticket_number, ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_net_profit, ss_ext_discount_amt, ss_coupon_amt, ss_ext_list_price from store_sales; d_date_sk, d_month_seq from date_dim; s_store_sk, s_store_name, s_manager from store. Joins: ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk, ss_store_sk = s_store_sk. Cohort month = MIN(d_month_seq) per customer and first store = the store of the first ticket. First-basket depth = (SUM(ss_ext_discount_amt) + SUM(ss_coupon_amt))/SUM(ss_ext_list_price) on the first ticket, bucketed into terciles. Build a matrix of months since acquisition (0 to 12) by cohort cell, holding average cumulative ss_net_profit per customer and the active share. Compute 1000-resample bootstrap confidence intervals and flag cells whose 12-month value falls below the store's median cohort with non-overlapping intervals. Output: s_store_name, s_manager, cohort_month, depth_tercile, cohort_size, cum_profit_m12, ci_low, ci_high, flag. ai_query writes the acquisition action plan per store.

use_cases.Name: Predict Shopper Lapse Risk with Prioritized Win-Back Outreach Queue
use_cases.Statement: Repeat shoppers who stop visiting are noticed only after their `ss_net_paid` has disappeared. Recency, frequency and spend-trend signals built from `ss_ticket_number` and `d_date` are not used to flag lapse risk early.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds monthly snapshot features per `ss_customer_sk`: recency, ticket frequency, `ss_net_paid` trend, `ss_coupon_amt` reliance and `c_preferred_cust_flag`. It trains a LightGBM classifier to predict no purchase in the next 90 days. It outputs a win-back outreach queue, ranked by lapse probability times trailing spend, for shoppers with a `c_email_address`.
use_cases.Business Value: The CRM Manager directs each week's win-back contacts to the highest-risk, highest-spend shoppers. This increases the share of flagged shoppers with a new `ss_ticket_number` within 90 days and protects trailing `ss_net_paid` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_net_paid`]. A holdout group makes the lift testable.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_customer_sk, ss_ticket_number, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_net_paid, ss_coupon_amt, ss_ext_discount_amt from store_sales; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim; c_customer_sk, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year, c_email_address from customer; i_item_sk, i_category from item. Joins: ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk, ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk, ss_item_sk = i_item_sk. Filter out rows with null ss_customer_sk. At each monthly snapshot, label = 1 if the customer has no ticket in the following 90 days. Features: recency_days; distinct ss_ticket_number counts over 90, 180 and 365 days; slope of monthly ss_net_paid; average basket value; distinct i_category count; coupon_ratio = SUM(ss_coupon_amt)/SUM(ss_net_paid); distinct ss_store_sk count; c_preferred_cust_flag; age derived from c_birth_year. Train LightGBM with num_leaves=31, learning_rate=0.05 and early stopping on a time-based split. Evaluate AUC and precision at the top decile, and compute SHAP values. Output: c_customer_sk, lapse_probability, spend_at_risk = trailing 12-month ss_net_paid times probability, top_drivers. ai_query turns each shopper's SHAP drivers into a recommended win-back message angle.

use_cases.Name: Accelerate Second Visits from First-Time Shoppers with Timed Follow-Up Schedule
use_cases.Statement: First-time shoppers, identified by their earliest store `ss_ticket_number` on `d_date`, either return or disappear. Without time-to-second-visit curves by first store and first `i_category`, marketing cannot time follow-up contact to the point where return likelihood starts to fall.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code derives each shopper's first and second distinct `ss_ticket_number` dates from `d_date` and censors shoppers with no return at the end of the data. It fits Kaplan-Meier curves and a Cox proportional hazards model on first-basket features such as `ss_net_paid`, first `i_category` and `c_preferred_cust_flag`. It outputs a timed follow-up schedule with a recommended contact day for each first-store and first-category segment.
use_cases.Business Value: The Lifecycle Marketing Manager schedules first-time shopper follow-ups at the day each segment's return hazard declines. This increases the share of first-time shoppers with a second `ss_ticket_number` within the chosen follow-up window [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_ticket_number`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_customer_sk, ss_ticket_number, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_net_paid, ss_ext_discount_amt, ss_ext_list_price from store_sales; d_date_sk, d_date, d_holiday from date_dim; i_item_sk, i_category from item; s_store_sk, s_store_name from store; c_customer_sk, c_preferred_cust_flag from customer. Joins: ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk, ss_item_sk = i_item_sk, ss_store_sk = s_store_sk, ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk. Per customer, rank distinct tickets by d_date. duration = days between the first and second ticket; event = 1 if a second ticket exists, else censored at MAX(d_date) of the dataset. First-basket covariates: SUM(ss_net_paid); line count; dominant i_category; s_store_name; discount_share = SUM(ss_ext_discount_amt)/SUM(ss_ext_list_price); first-day d_holiday; c_preferred_cust_flag. Fit Kaplan-Meier curves per segment and a Cox PH model (lifelines, penalizer=0.1) and check proportional hazards with Schoenfeld residuals. Output: segment (first store x first category), median_days_to_return, hazard_drop_day, recommended_contact_day, top hazard ratios. ai_query writes follow-up timing guidance and offer framing per segment.

use_cases.Name: Predict Catalog Customer Lapse Timing with Reactivation Outreach Queue
use_cases.Statement: Repeat buyers identified by `cs_bill_customer_sk` stop ordering (no new `cs_order_number`) without warning. Marketing contacts them only after a long silence, by which point their typical `cs_net_paid` spend is already lost.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds each customer's order timeline from `cs_order_number` and sold dates and fits a Cox proportional hazards model of time to next order. Covariates are drawn from order value and `c_preferred_cust_flag`. The final output is a reactivation outreach queue ranked by expected revenue at risk.
use_cases.Business Value: The CRM Manager contacts customers whose return probability is dropping before they lapse. The goal is to increase the repeat-order rate (new `cs_order_number` per `cs_bill_customer_sk`) and recover repeat `cs_net_paid` [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_net_paid`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_ship_customer_sk, cs_order_number, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_net_paid from catalog_sales; c_customer_sk, c_customer_id, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year, c_email_address from customer; d_date_sk, d_date, d_year from date_dim. Joins: customer ON cs_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk; date_dim ON cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Collapse to order level by cs_order_number and compute inter-order gaps per customer. The event is the next order; gaps still open at MAX(d_date) are right-censored. Covariates: orders_to_date, avg_order_value = AVG(SUM(cs_net_paid) per order), gift_share = share of orders where cs_bill_customer_sk <> cs_ship_customer_sk, age = d_year - c_birth_year, and c_preferred_cust_flag. Fit lifelines CoxPHFitter with penalizer=0.1 and check proportional hazards. Score S(90 days) for each active customer and compute revenue_at_risk = avg_order_value * (1 - S90). Output schema: (c_customer_id, days_since_last_order, prob_return_90d, revenue_at_risk, top_hazard_drivers). As a final step, ai_query writes a reactivation recommendation for each queued customer.

use_cases.Name: Prioritize Web Sites by Acquired Customer Retention with Acquisition Focus Plan
use_cases.Statement: Each customer's first web order lands on a specific `ws_web_site_sk`. Sites likely differ in whether those first-time buyers return, measured by repeat `ws_order_number` and cumulative `ws_net_profit`, but acquisition effort is not steered by that difference.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `web_sales` to `web_site` on `ws_web_site_sk` = `web_site_sk` and to `date_dim` on `ws_sold_date_sk` = `d_date_sk`. It assigns each `ws_bill_customer_sk` to an acquisition month and acquiring site, then builds 12-month retention and cumulative profit curves per site-cohort with bootstrap intervals. The output is an acquisition focus plan that ranks sites, with an increase-focus or fix-onboarding action for each.
use_cases.Business Value: The Customer Acquisition Manager shifts acquisition effort toward sites whose new buyers return more often. This increases repeat-buyer rate and 12-month `ws_net_profit` per acquired customer [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_net_profit`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_web_site_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_sold_time_sk, ws_order_number, ws_net_profit from web_sales; web_site_sk, web_name, web_market_manager from web_site; d_date_sk, d_date, d_month_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) JOIN ON ws_web_site_sk = web_site_sk and ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) For each ws_bill_customer_sk, the first order (MIN d_date, tie-break MIN ws_sold_time_sk) sets cohort_month = d_month_seq and the acquiring site. (3) For months 1 to 12 after acquisition, compute the cohort share with any order on any site and the cumulative SUM(ws_net_profit) per acquired customer. (4) Compare sites within the same cohort months using month-3 and month-6 retention and 12-month profit, with 500-resample bootstrap intervals; with only 30 sites, report the interval width. (5) Output: web_name, web_market_manager, cohort_size, m3_retention, m6_retention, profit_per_acquired_customer, rank, action. (6) ai_query receives each site's curves and writes the focus or onboarding-fix recommendation.

use_cases.Name: Predict Early First Returns by New Customers with Onboarding Outreach Queue
use_cases.Statement: Customers who return soon after their first purchase (`c_first_sales_date_sk`) drive avoidable `sr_net_loss`. Marketing cannot tell which newly acquired customers are likely to return early.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code models time from `c_first_sales_date_sk` to each customer's first `sr_returned_date_sk` with a Cox proportional hazards model, treating customers with no return as censored. The output is an onboarding outreach queue of new customers ranked by early-return hazard.
use_cases.Business Value: The CRM Manager sends guidance and fit-help outreach to the top of the queue. The goal is to reduce early-return counts and first-return `sr_net_loss` among new customers [ESTIMATE: depends on `sr_net_loss`]. Impact is measured by comparing a treated group against a randomized holdout.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: sr_customer_sk, sr_returned_date_sk, sr_net_loss from store_returns; c_customer_sk, c_first_sales_date_sk, c_first_shipto_date_sk, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year, c_birth_country, c_email_address from customer. Approach: (1) LEFT JOIN customer to a per-customer MIN(sr_returned_date_sk) subquery ON c_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk. (2) duration = first_return_sk - c_first_sales_date_sk [ASSUMPTION: date keys are sequential day numbers]. event = 1 if a return exists; otherwise duration = MAX(sr_returned_date_sk) - c_first_sales_date_sk with event = 0. Drop negative durations. (3) Covariates: c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year, c_birth_country (top 20 levels plus other), has_email = c_email_address IS NOT NULL, shipto_gap = c_first_shipto_date_sk - c_first_sales_date_sk. (4) Fit Kaplan-Meier curves for a baseline view, then lifelines CoxPH with penalizer=0.1. Check proportional hazards with Schoenfeld residuals. (5) Output schema: c_customer_sk, 90-day early-return probability, top hazard drivers. (6) ai_query writes a personalized outreach reason per customer, producing the onboarding outreach queue.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Free-Shipping Thresholds with Shipping Charge Policy Recommendation
use_cases.Statement: The shipping amount customers pay, derived as `ws_net_paid_inc_ship` minus `ws_net_paid`, and the shipping cost borne, `ws_ext_ship_cost`, are not used to test what a free-shipping threshold would cost. Policy is set without a break-even view.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `web_sales` to `date_dim` on `ws_sold_date_sk` = `d_date_sk` and to `ship_mode` on `ws_ship_mode_sk` = `sm_ship_mode_sk`. For each candidate order-value threshold, it runs a Monte Carlo resampling of historical orders to estimate waived shipping charges, and it computes the break-even share of near-threshold orders that would need to trade up. The output is a shipping charge policy recommendation listing threshold, waived-charge distribution and break-even trade-up rate.
use_cases.Business Value: The E-Commerce Finance Manager chooses a threshold whose break-even trade-up rate is attainable. This reduces waived shipping charges per order and protects `ws_net_profit` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_net_paid_inc_ship`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_order_number, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_ship_mode_sk, ws_net_paid, ws_net_paid_inc_ship, ws_ext_ship_cost, ws_net_profit from web_sales; d_date_sk, d_moy from date_dim; sm_ship_mode_sk, sm_type from ship_mode. Approach: (1) JOIN ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and ON ws_ship_mode_sk = sm_ship_mode_sk. (2) Aggregate per ws_order_number: merch = SUM(ws_net_paid), ship_charged = SUM(ws_net_paid_inc_ship - ws_net_paid), ship_cost = SUM(ws_ext_ship_cost), profit = SUM(ws_net_profit), plus d_moy and sm_type. (3) Build the candidate threshold grid from deciles of merch. (4) Monte Carlo with 10,000 bootstrap draws of month-specific order sets: waive ship_charged for orders with merch at or above the threshold. Compute waived charges and, for orders in a band just below the threshold, the break-even trade-up share needed for their margin gain to offset waived charges, using profit/merch margin from the data. The trade-up rate is reported as an output, not assumed. (5) Output: threshold, sm_type scope, expected_waived, p5, p95, break_even_tradeup_share. (6) ai_query receives the scenario table and writes the policy recommendation and its key risk.

use_cases.Name: Recalibrate Catalog Shipping Charges by Order Profile with Shipping Rate Card Update
use_cases.Statement: Shipping cost in `cs_ext_ship_cost` varies with `cs_quantity`, ship mode and warehouse. The shipping charged to customers, derived as `cs_net_paid_inc_ship` minus `cs_net_paid`, may not track that cost for each order profile, which erodes `cs_net_profit` on costly order types.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code fits a Ridge regression of order-level `cs_ext_ship_cost` on quantity, line count, `i_category`, `sm_type`, `sm_carrier` and warehouse. It compares predicted cost with the derived charged shipping for each profile, and ai_query drafts rate changes with a short justification. The output is a shipping rate card update listing the order profiles whose charges should be raised or lowered.
use_cases.Business Value: The Fulfillment Pricing Analyst revises the shipping rate card for each order profile. This should shrink the gap between derived charged shipping and `cs_ext_ship_cost` and increase `cs_net_profit` on under-charged profiles [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_ext_ship_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_order_number, cs_warehouse_sk, cs_ship_mode_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_quantity, cs_list_price, cs_ext_ship_cost, cs_net_paid, cs_net_paid_inc_ship, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; sm_ship_mode_sk, sm_type, sm_carrier from ship_mode; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_sq_ft from warehouse; i_item_sk, i_category from item. Approach: JOIN cs_ship_mode_sk = sm_ship_mode_sk, cs_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk and cs_item_sk = i_item_sk. Aggregate per cs_order_number x cs_warehouse_sk x cs_ship_mode_sk: total_qty, line_count, ship_cost = SUM(cs_ext_ship_cost), charged_ship = SUM(cs_net_paid_inc_ship - cs_net_paid), dominant i_category and avg cs_list_price. Fit Ridge (alpha=1.0, 5-fold CV) with one-hot sm_type, sm_carrier, cs_warehouse_sk and i_category plus standardized numerics. Compute charge_gap = charged_ship - predicted_cost. Group into profiles (sm_type x i_category x quantity band) and rank by the sum of negative gaps. Output schema: profile, orders, mean_predicted_cost, mean_charged, gap, recommended_direction. Final step: ai_query turns the coefficients and gaps into rate-card change recommendations.

use_cases.Name: Reduce Split Shipments in Multi-Line Catalog Orders with Stock Co-Location Plan
use_cases.Statement: Some catalog orders identified by `cs_order_number` have lines shipped from more than one `cs_warehouse_sk` or on different `cs_ship_date_sk` dates. These orders carry extra `cs_ext_ship_cost`, and the item classes that cause the splits are unknown.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code flags split orders and attributes their incremental shipping cost to the item class and warehouse pair that caused each split. It then ranks those pairs with a Pareto cut on cumulative cost, and ai_query drafts the co-location rationale. The output is a stock co-location plan listing which item classes to also stock in the warehouse that ships the rest of the order.
use_cases.Business Value: The Network Inventory Planner uses the plan to change stocking locations for the top split-driving item classes. This should reduce the share of split orders and `cs_ext_ship_cost` per order [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_ext_ship_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_order_number, cs_item_sk, cs_warehouse_sk, cs_ship_date_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_quantity, cs_ext_sales_price, cs_ext_ship_cost from catalog_sales; i_item_sk, i_class, i_category from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim. Approach: JOIN cs_item_sk = i_item_sk, cs_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk, and cs_ship_date_sk and cs_sold_date_sk to d_date_sk. Per order, compute n_wh = COUNT(DISTINCT cs_warehouse_sk) and n_ship_dates = COUNT(DISTINCT cs_ship_date_sk); split = n_wh > 1 OR n_ship_dates > 1. The primary warehouse is the one with the largest cs_ext_sales_price share; lines from other warehouses are split drivers. Incremental cost = ship cost per unit on split orders minus the median ship cost per unit on single-warehouse orders with the same line count. Group driver lines by i_class x (primary w_warehouse_name, off-primary w_warehouse_name), sort by incremental cost and keep pairs up to 80 percent cumulative share. [MISSING_DATA: on-hand stock by warehouse] is needed to confirm feasibility. Output schema: i_class, primary_warehouse, source_warehouse, split_orders, incremental_cost, cumulative_share. Final step: ai_query writes the co-location recommendation for each pair.

use_cases.Name: Simulate Warehouse Network Consolidation with Footprint Decision Recommendation
use_cases.Statement: Stock density, measured as `inv_quantity_on_hand` per `w_warehouse_sq_ft`, varies across the warehouse network. Leadership lacks evidence on whether one site's stock could be absorbed by the others, in the same `w_city` or nearby, without exceeding observed peak densities.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code runs a Monte Carlo simulation that resamples weekly on-hand by warehouse and category over `d_week_seq`. For each candidate closure, it reallocates the closed site's units to the remaining sites and measures the probability of exceeding historical peak density. The output is a footprint decision recommendation ranking closure scenarios by overflow risk.
use_cases.Business Value: The Network Strategy Director decides which warehouse, if any, to consolidate. The KPIs are higher units per `w_warehouse_sq_ft` across the network and a lower simulated probability of density overflow [ESTIMATE: depends on `w_warehouse_sq_ft`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name, w_warehouse_sq_ft, w_city from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_moy from date_dim; i_item_sk, i_category from item. Join on inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk, inv_date_sk = d_date_sk and inv_item_sk = i_item_sk. Feature engineering: weekly_units per warehouse and category; density = weekly_units / w_warehouse_sq_ft; peak_density = P95 density observed per warehouse. Simulation: 10,000 Monte Carlo runs using a 4-week block bootstrap over d_week_seq to preserve cross-warehouse co-movement. For each scenario (close warehouse j, or no closure), reassign j's units to sites in the same w_city first, then to others, in proportion to their free headroom = peak_density times w_warehouse_sq_ft minus weekly_units. Record P(any site exceeds its peak_density) and the peak-week overflow units by d_moy. Output: scenario, receiving sites, overflow_probability, P95 overflow_units, network units per sq ft. ai_query then explains the trade-offs of each scenario and recommends a footprint decision.

use_cases.Name: Reduce Excess Return Shipping Charges by Store with Freight Recovery List
use_cases.Statement: Return shipping cost (`sr_return_ship_cost`) varies by store beyond what `sr_return_quantity`, item category and units explain. This points to stores overpaying or miscoding return freight.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code fits a Ridge regression of `sr_return_ship_cost` on quantity, amount and item attributes, then aggregates residuals by store and item class. The output is a freight recovery list of store and class combinations with persistent excess shipping cost.
use_cases.Business Value: The Reverse Logistics Manager challenges freight charges for the stores on the list. The goal is to reduce excess `sr_return_ship_cost` above the model's expected value [ESTIMATE: depends on `sr_return_ship_cost`]. Impact is measured by comparing residual trends before and after intervention.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: sr_store_sk, sr_item_sk, sr_returned_date_sk, sr_return_quantity, sr_return_amt, sr_return_ship_cost from store_returns; i_item_sk, i_category, i_class, i_size, i_units, i_current_price from item; s_store_sk, s_store_name, s_state, s_floor_space from store. Approach: (1) JOIN item ON sr_item_sk = i_item_sk and JOIN store ON sr_store_sk = s_store_sk. (2) Features: log(sr_return_quantity), log(sr_return_amt), i_current_price, one-hot i_category/i_class/i_size/i_units. Store is deliberately excluded so residuals capture store effects. (3) Fit Ridge regression with alpha=1.0 and 5-fold CV. (4) Compute residual = actual - predicted sr_return_ship_cost. Aggregate by s_store_name x i_class with mean residual, total excess and a t-test on persistence across week buckets FLOOR(sr_returned_date_sk/7). (5) Output schema: s_store_name, i_class, total_excess_cost, mean_residual, p_value. (6) ai_query explains each excess pattern and recommends recovery actions, producing the freight recovery list sorted by total_excess_cost.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Returnless Refund Thresholds by Item Class with Refund Routing Rules
use_cases.Statement: For many low-value web returns, `wr_return_ship_cost` may approach or exceed the merchandise value being recovered, measured as `i_wholesale_cost` times `wr_return_quantity`. Despite this, every return is shipped back by default.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code compares return shipping cost with recovered item value for each return. It optimizes a per-`i_class` refund-amount threshold below which a refund is issued without physical return, subject to a cap on the returnless share and an exclusion for frequent returners identified from `wr_returning_customer_sk` history. The final deliverable is a set of refund routing rules listing the threshold per class and the projected savings.
use_cases.Business Value: The Reverse Logistics Manager loads the routing rules into refund handling and reviews them quarterly. This reduces total `wr_return_ship_cost` net of forgone recovered value [ESTIMATE: depends on wr_return_ship_cost].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: wr_item_sk, wr_reason_sk, wr_returning_customer_sk, wr_returned_date_sk, wr_return_quantity, wr_return_amt, wr_return_ship_cost, wr_net_loss from web_returns; i_item_sk, i_class, i_category, i_wholesale_cost from item; r_reason_sk, r_reason_desc from reason. Approach: JOIN item ON wr_item_sk = i_item_sk and JOIN reason ON wr_reason_sk = r_reason_sk. For each return, set recovery_value = i_wholesale_cost * wr_return_quantity, used as a proxy [MISSING_DATA: actual resale or disposition value], and handling_cost = wr_return_ship_cost. For each i_class, define the decision variable t_c as a threshold on wr_return_amt; returns at or below t_c route to returnless. The objective is to maximize SUM(handling_cost - recovery_value) over routed returns. Constraints: the returnless share per class is at or below a planner cap; returning customers in the top decile of return count are excluded; reasons chosen by the planner from r_reason_desc are excluded. Solve with a grid search over 20 quantiles of wr_return_amt per class. Validate on the later half of the wr_returned_date_sk range to check that savings persist. Output columns: i_class, t_c, routed share and projected net savings. As the final step, ai_query writes the routing rule rationale per class and flags classes where savings are unstable.

use_cases.Name: Detect Abnormal Store Sales Drops with Store Operations Investigation Queue
use_cases.Statement: A store-day where `ss_net_paid` or ticket count from `ss_ticket_number` falls well below what its `d_dow` and `d_holiday` pattern predicts may indicate an operational disruption such as lost trading hours. Daily totals are reviewed only in aggregate, so these drops go unnoticed.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code fits expected daily `ss_net_paid` and ticket counts per store with Prophet. It then runs an Isolation Forest on the residuals together with average basket value and hours with sales (`t_hour` coverage versus `s_hours`).
