(2) Compute line gap_ratio = (ws_wholesale_cost - i_wholesale_cost)/i_wholesale_cost and gap_dollars = (ws_wholesale_cost - i_wholesale_cost)*ws_quantity. (3) Aggregate per i_manufact_id and d_week_seq: mean gap_ratio, share of positive-gap lines, SUM(gap_dollars), gap_ratio stddev, distinct items affected. (4) Score with Isolation Forest (contamination=0.03) and LOF (n_neighbors=20), then average the rank-normalized scores. (5) Output: i_manufact, d_week_seq, gap_dollars, items_affected, ensemble_score. (6) ai_query receives each flagged manufacturer-week with its top items and writes an audit brief and credit request summary.

use_cases.Name: Prevent Sales Tax Collection Errors by Web Site with Tax Correction Queue
use_cases.Statement: Tax collected per line (`ws_ext_tax`) should follow the site's `web_tax_percentage` applied to `ws_net_paid`. Persistent gaps by site, state or category signal either under-collection liability or overcharging of customers.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `web_sales` to `web_site` on `ws_web_site_sk` = `web_site_sk`, to `item` on `ws_item_sk` = `i_item_sk` and to `date_dim` on `ws_sold_date_sk` = `d_date_sk`. It derives the expected tax from `ws_net_paid` and `web_tax_percentage`, cross-checks the result against `ws_net_paid_inc_tax`, and scores site-category-month gap profiles with an Isolation Forest. The output is a tax correction queue listing the direction and amount of each flagged gap.
use_cases.Business Value: The Tax Compliance Manager corrects tax setup for flagged site and category combinations every month. This reduces under-collected tax liability and over-collected amounts computed from `ws_ext_tax` versus expected tax [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_ext_tax`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_web_site_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_ext_tax, ws_net_paid, ws_net_paid_inc_tax from web_sales; web_site_sk, web_site_id, web_state, web_tax_percentage from web_site; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_month_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) Perform the three JOINs on the keys listed above. (2) Compute expected_tax = ws_net_paid * web_tax_percentage; confirm whether web_tax_percentage is stored as a fraction or a percent. (3) Compute gap = ws_ext_tax - expected_tax and consistency = (ws_net_paid_inc_tax - ws_net_paid) - ws_ext_tax. (4) Aggregate per web_site_id, i_category and d_month_seq: signed gap sum, absolute gap rate, share of lines beyond rounding tolerance, month-over-month gap change, consistency breaks. (5) Train an Isolation Forest (contamination=0.03) on these features. (6) Output: web_site_id, web_state, i_category, d_month_seq, under_collected, over_collected, anomaly_score. (7) ai_query receives each flagged row and drafts a correction note stating the likely configuration cause.

use_cases.Name: Identify Brand Pairs Bought and Returned Together with Product Comparison Content Plan
use_cases.Statement: Orders in which several items from the same `i_class_id` but different `i_brand_id` are returned under one `wr_order_number` suggest customers are buying alternatives to compare and then sending most of them back. The resulting `wr_net_loss` and `wr_return_ship_cost` are spread invisibly across brands.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds an item co-return graph whose edges link items returned in the same `wr_order_number`, filtered to same-class, different-brand pairs and weighted by order count. It runs label propagation for communities and PageRank for hub items. The final deliverable is a product comparison content plan that ranks the item communities and hub listings most in need of side-by-side comparison content.
use_cases.Business Value: The Ecommerce Merchandising Manager adds comparison content to the top-ranked hub listings and reviews duplicated assortment in each community. This reduces co-returned order counts and their combined `wr_net_loss` and `wr_return_ship_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on wr_net_loss].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: wr_order_number, wr_item_sk, wr_return_quantity, wr_return_amt, wr_return_ship_cost, wr_net_loss from web_returns; i_item_sk, i_class_id, i_class, i_brand_id, i_brand, i_category, i_current_price from item. Approach: JOIN item ON wr_item_sk = i_item_sk. Self-join web_returns on wr_order_number to form item pairs (a.wr_item_sk < b.wr_item_sk), keeping pairs that share i_class_id and differ in i_brand_id. Set edge weight = distinct co-return orders and edge loss = SUM(wr_net_loss + wr_return_ship_cost) across the pair. Keep edges with weight of 3 or more. In GraphFrames, run labelPropagation (maxIter=10) for communities and PageRank (resetProbability=0.15) for hub items. Output a ranked list of communities with member items, brands, co-return order count, combined loss and hub item. As the final step, ai_query drafts per-community content recommendations, such as a comparison table for the hub listing and a duplicate-assortment review.

use_cases.Name: Detect Category Margin Compression with Repricing Action List
use_cases.Statement: Gross margin, from `ss_ext_sales_price` versus `ss_ext_wholesale_cost` (and the catalog and web equivalents), can drift down within an `i_class` for weeks before anyone notices. It is also unclear whether rising wholesale cost or falling selling price is the cause.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code computes weekly margin per `i_category` and `i_class` across all channels, decomposes it with STL, and runs change-point detection on the trend. It attributes each shift to `ss_wholesale_cost` versus `ss_sales_price` movement. The output is a repricing action list per affected class.
use_cases.Business Value: The Category Finance Analyst acts on margin breaks within weeks of their start. This recovers gross margin, computed from `ss_ext_sales_price` minus `ss_ext_wholesale_cost`, on affected classes [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_ext_wholesale_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_sold_date_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_quantity, ss_sales_price, ss_wholesale_cost, ss_ext_sales_price, ss_ext_wholesale_cost from store_sales; cs_sold_date_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_ext_sales_price, cs_ext_wholesale_cost from catalog_sales; ws_sold_date_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_ext_sales_price, ws_ext_wholesale_cost from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_category, i_class from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) UNION the channels and JOIN item ON *_item_sk = i_item_sk and date_dim ON *_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Weekly margin per i_category x i_class = (SUM(ext_sales_price) - SUM(ext_wholesale_cost)) / SUM(ext_sales_price). (3) STL decomposition (period=52, robust=true), then the ruptures PELT change-point method on the trend component (rbf cost, penalty chosen by BIC). (4) For each downward break, attribute the margin delta into a unit cost effect (change in avg ss_wholesale_cost), a price effect (change in avg ss_sales_price) and a mix effect, using a standard price-volume-mix decomposition. Output: i_category, i_class, break_week, margin_before, margin_after, cost_effect, price_effect, mix_effect, channel. Final step: ai_query writes a repricing or cost-renegotiation action per class based on the dominant driver.

use_cases.Name: Detect Cross-Channel Price Inconsistencies with Price Harmonization Actions
use_cases.Statement: The same item can sell at very different realized prices across channels in the same week, comparing `ss_sales_price`, `cs_sales_price` and `ws_sales_price` against `i_current_price`. This leaks `cs_net_profit` and `ws_net_profit` when one channel undercuts the others.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds item-week vectors of channel price ratios to `i_current_price` and channel discount ratios, and scores them with Local Outlier Factor against each category's normal pattern. The output is a list of price harmonization actions naming the underpriced channel.
use_cases.Business Value: The Channel Pricing Manager corrects flagged item-weeks where one channel is out of line. This reduces net profit leakage on flagged items, measured on `ws_net_profit` and `cs_net_profit` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_sales_price`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_sold_date_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_sales_price, ss_list_price, ss_quantity, ss_net_profit from store_sales; cs_sold_date_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_sales_price, cs_list_price, cs_quantity, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; ws_sold_date_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_sales_price, ws_list_price, ws_quantity, ws_net_profit from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_category, i_current_price from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) JOIN each channel to date_dim ON *_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and to item ON *_item_sk = i_item_sk. (2) Per i_item_sk x d_week_seq x channel, compute quantity-weighted avg sales_price and list_price. (3) Pivot to a vector per item-week: store_ratio, catalog_ratio, web_ratio = avg sales_price / i_current_price; per-channel discount = 1 - sales_price / list_price; max_min_spread = max ratio - min ratio. Keep item-weeks sold in at least two channels. (4) Fit LocalOutlierFactor (n_neighbors=20, contamination=0.02) per i_category on the standardized vectors. (5) Identify the underpriced channel as the lowest ratio. profit_at_risk = (peer channel price - channel price) x channel quantity. Output: i_item_id, d_week_seq, lof_score, underpriced_channel, ratios, profit_at_risk. Final step: ai_query writes a harmonization action per flagged item-week (align price, end discount, verify catalog print price).

use_cases.Name: Detect Realized Price Erosion by Category with Markdown Governance Alerts
use_cases.Statement: The realized price ratio (`ws_ext_sales_price` relative to `ws_ext_list_price`) can drift down slowly in some `i_category` and `i_brand` groups. The drift hides inside seasonal swings, so margin erodes before anyone notices.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds a monthly realized price index per category and brand on `d_month_seq`. It removes seasonality with STL decomposition and locates structural breaks with change-point detection. The output is a markdown governance alert list naming the brand, break month and erosion slope.
use_cases.Business Value: The Merchandise Finance Analyst escalates brands with a confirmed downward break for markdown review. This prevents further decline in the realized price ratio and protects `ws_net_profit` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_ext_discount_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_item_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_ext_sales_price, ws_ext_list_price, ws_ext_discount_amt, ws_net_profit from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_category, i_brand from item; d_date_sk, d_month_seq from date_dim. Joins: JOIN item ON ws_item_sk = i_item_sk; JOIN date_dim ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Monthly series per i_category x i_brand: realized price index = sum ws_ext_sales_price / sum ws_ext_list_price, plus profit margin = sum ws_net_profit / sum ws_ext_sales_price. Apply STL decomposition (period=12, robust=true). Run PELT change-point detection (ruptures, rbf cost, BIC penalty) on the trend component, and a Mann-Kendall test with Sen slope after the last break. Output: i_category, i_brand, break d_month_seq, pre and post index levels, slope, alert flag. Final step: ai_query summarizes each alert and recommends the markdown review action.

use_cases.Name: Predict Unit Response to Markdowns with Category Pricing Guidelines
use_cases.Statement: Markdowns, seen as the gap between `ws_sales_price` and `ws_list_price`, are applied with the same depth across every `i_category`. Nobody knows how much extra `ws_quantity` each markdown actually buys, so some categories give away margin while others leave volume on the table.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code fits log-log Ridge regressions of weekly `ws_quantity` on the realized price ratio `ws_sales_price` / `ws_list_price` per `i_category`, controlling for `d_holiday` and season. Each category's elasticity is combined with `ws_wholesale_cost` to find the margin-maximizing markdown depth. The output is a per-category pricing guideline sheet.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager sets markdown depth per category from measured unit response instead of uniform rules. This increases `ws_net_profit` per unit sold and reduces discount dollars in `ws_ext_discount_amt` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_ext_discount_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_item_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_quantity, ws_sales_price, ws_list_price, ws_wholesale_cost, ws_ext_discount_amt, ws_net_profit from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_category, i_class from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_moy, d_holiday from date_dim. Joins: JOIN item ON ws_item_sk = i_item_sk; JOIN date_dim ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Aggregate per i_item_id x d_week_seq: units, average realized price ratio = avg(ws_sales_price / ws_list_price), and average ws_list_price. Model per i_category: Ridge regression (alpha=1.0) of log(units) on log(price ratio), log(list price), a holiday-week flag and d_moy dummies, with item fixed effects demeaned. Bootstrap 200 resamples to get elasticity confidence intervals. Solve for the price ratio that maximizes (ws_sales_price - ws_wholesale_cost) x predicted units. Output: i_category, elasticity, ci_low, ci_high, recommended price ratio. Final step: ai_query writes a pricing guideline per category explaining the trade-off.

use_cases.Name: Detect Unrecovered Cost Increases by Item Class with Price Adjustment Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: When unit `ss_wholesale_cost` rises for an `i_class`, `ss_sales_price` may not follow, silently compressing `ss_net_profit`. Buyers have no view of which classes show weak or lagging co-movement between cost and selling price.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code computes monthly unit cost and unit price per `i_class` from `ss_ext_wholesale_cost`, `ss_ext_sales_price` and `ss_quantity`. It measures rolling and lagged correlation of their changes with permutation significance tests and outputs a price adjustment recommendation list for classes where cost rose without matching price movement, alongside the current `i_current_price`.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager prioritizes price reviews for classes with unrecovered cost increases. This reduces the decline in `ss_net_profit`/`ss_ext_sales_price` margin for those classes [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_ext_wholesale_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_quantity, ss_ext_wholesale_cost, ss_ext_sales_price, ss_net_profit from store_sales; i_item_sk, i_class, i_category, i_current_price, i_manager_id from item; d_date_sk, d_month_seq from date_dim. Joins: ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Per (i_class, d_month_seq): unit_cost = SUM(ss_ext_wholesale_cost)/SUM(ss_quantity), unit_price = SUM(ss_ext_sales_price)/SUM(ss_quantity), margin = SUM(ss_net_profit)/SUM(ss_ext_sales_price). Compute month-over-month log changes, a rolling 12-month Spearman correlation, and cross-correlation at lags 0 to 3 months with 1000-permutation p-values. Flag classes with a rising cumulative unit cost, no significant positive correlation at any lag, and a declining margin trend. Output: i_class, i_category, i_manager_id, cost_change, price_change, best_lag_corr, p_value, margin_change, avg i_current_price. ai_query writes a price adjustment recommendation per flagged class.

use_cases.Name: Predict Loss-Making Sale Lines with Pricing Rule Corrections
use_cases.Statement: Line items with negative `ss_net_profit` occur when realized price after `ss_coupon_amt` falls below `ss_wholesale_cost`. The combinations of category, promotion presence (`ss_promo_sk`), store and hour that systematically produce them are unknown before the sale.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code trains an XGBoost classifier on context known before checkout: `i_category`, `i_class`, the `i_current_price`/`i_wholesale_cost` markup, promotion presence, store, `t_hour`, `d_dow`, `d_holiday` and `ss_quantity`. It predicts the probability that a line sells at a loss, uses SHAP to rank risky combinations, and delivers pricing rule corrections such as coupon-stacking limits or price floors per combination.
use_cases.Business Value: The Merchandise Financial Planner enacts pricing rule corrections for the highest-risk combinations. This reduces the share of lines with negative `ss_net_profit` and the total loss on them [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_net_profit`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_sold_time_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_promo_sk, ss_quantity, ss_net_profit, ss_coupon_amt from store_sales; i_item_sk, i_category, i_class, i_brand_id, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost from item; s_store_sk, s_store_name from store; t_time_sk, t_hour from time_dim; d_date_sk, d_dow, d_holiday, d_moy from date_dim. Joins: ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk, ss_store_sk = s_store_sk, ss_sold_time_sk = t_time_sk, ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Label = ss_net_profit < 0. Features exclude realized price and discount fields to avoid leakage: promo_flag (ss_promo_sk not null), markup = i_current_price/i_wholesale_cost, i_category, i_class, i_brand_id, s_store_name, t_hour, d_dow, d_holiday, d_moy, ss_quantity. Train XGBoost with max_depth=6, eta=0.1, n_estimators=400 and scale_pos_weight set to the class ratio, using a time-based split, and evaluate AUC and calibration. Aggregate SHAP values to (i_class, promo_flag, s_store_name) combinations and attach the observed loss sum and the share of losses involving ss_coupon_amt > 0. Output: combination, predicted_loss_rate, observed_loss_sum, top_drivers, proposed_rule. ai_query drafts each pricing rule correction with its justification.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Markdown Depth by Item Class with Pricing Recalibration Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: Markdowns from `ss_list_price` to `ss_sales_price` are applied without knowing how much `ss_quantity` actually responds in each `i_class`. Some classes may be discounted beyond the point where extra volume offsets the lost `ss_net_profit`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code fits a log-log Ridge regression per `i_class` of weekly `ss_quantity` on the realized price ratio `ss_sales_price`/`ss_list_price`, controlling for store, `d_moy`, holiday weeks and promotion presence from `ss_promo_sk`. It converts the price coefficients into profit-maximizing markdown depths using `ss_wholesale_cost` and delivers a pricing recalibration list per class.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager resets markdown depth for classes with low price response. This reduces `ss_ext_discount_amt` and increases `ss_net_profit` per unit sold in those classes, testable by staggering the rollout across stores [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_ext_discount_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_sales_price, ss_wholesale_cost, ss_promo_sk, ss_ext_discount_amt, ss_net_profit from store_sales; i_item_sk, i_class, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_moy, d_holiday from date_dim; s_store_sk, s_store_name from store. Joins: ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk, ss_store_sk = s_store_sk. Aggregate to (i_class, s_store_name, d_week_seq) with units = SUM(ss_quantity), price_ratio = AVG(ss_sales_price/ss_list_price) weighted by quantity, promo_share = share of lines with non-null ss_promo_sk, holiday flag, d_moy. Fit Ridge regression of log(units) on log(price_ratio) plus store one-hot, d_moy one-hot, holiday and promo_share, with alpha=1.0 and 5-fold time-series CV. Take the log(price_ratio) coefficient as the class price response. Compute the profit-maximizing price ratio given the average ss_wholesale_cost/ss_list_price and compare it to the current average. Output: i_class, price_response, current_avg_markdown, recommended_markdown, expected_profit_change_direction, CV R2. ai_query explains each class's recommendation and flags low-confidence fits.

use_cases.Name: Predict Loss-Making Orders at Quote Stage with Discount Approval Guardrails
use_cases.Statement: Order lines with negative `cs_net_profit` are discovered only after shipping. Yet contextual signals known at quote time, such as `cs_list_price` relative to `cs_wholesale_cost`, ship mode and `cs_quantity`, could flag them earlier.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code trains an XGBoost classifier for `cs_net_profit` < 0. To avoid leakage, it uses only quote-stage features (`cs_quantity`, `cs_list_price`, `cs_wholesale_cost`, `cs_ext_ship_cost`, item, ship mode, warehouse, call center, month) and excludes realized price, discount and paid columns. The final output is a scored order list plus a discount approval guardrail rule table built from SHAP drivers.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager requires approval before discounting high-risk quote contexts. The goal is to reduce the count and value of order lines with negative `cs_net_profit` [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_net_profit`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_order_number, cs_item_sk, cs_ship_mode_sk, cs_warehouse_sk, cs_call_center_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_quantity, cs_list_price, cs_wholesale_cost, cs_ext_ship_cost, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; i_item_sk, i_category, i_brand_id from item; sm_ship_mode_sk, sm_type, sm_carrier from ship_mode; w_warehouse_sk from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_date, d_moy, d_holiday from date_dim. Joins: item ON cs_item_sk = i_item_sk; ship_mode ON cs_ship_mode_sk = sm_ship_mode_sk; warehouse ON cs_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk; date_dim ON cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Label: cs_net_profit < 0. Features: markup = cs_list_price/cs_wholesale_cost, ship_cost_per_unit = cs_ext_ship_cost/cs_quantity, cs_quantity, i_category, i_brand_id, sm_type, sm_carrier, cs_warehouse_sk, cs_call_center_sk, d_moy, d_holiday. Train XGBoost with max_depth=6, eta=0.1, 400 rounds and scale_pos_weight set by class ratio, using a time split on d_date; evaluate with AUC-PR, track in MLflow and explain with SHAP. Output schema: (cs_order_number, cs_item_sk, loss_probability, top_shap_drivers) plus a guardrail table of (context, risk_rate). As a final step, ai_query converts the SHAP patterns into discount approval rules.

use_cases.Name: Simulate Discount Cap Scenarios by Category with Pricing Policy Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: Deep markdowns, measured as `cs_sales_price` below `cs_list_price`, vary widely by `i_category`. The business cannot see how capping discount depth would change `cs_net_profit` given the observed shifts in `cs_quantity` across discount bands.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds empirical quantity distributions per category and discount band from `cs_quantity`, then runs a Monte Carlo simulation of discount cap scenarios that recomputes margin using `cs_wholesale_cost` and `cs_ext_ship_cost`. The final output is a pricing policy recommendation per category with P10/P50/P90 profit bands.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager sets category discount caps based on the scenario with the best downside-protected `cs_net_profit` [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_net_profit`]. Results are verified by comparing post-policy margin against prior periods.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_item_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_quantity, cs_list_price, cs_sales_price, cs_wholesale_cost, cs_ext_ship_cost, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_moy from date_dim. Joins: item ON cs_item_sk = i_item_sk; date_dim ON cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Compute discount_depth = 1 - cs_sales_price/cs_list_price, bin it into deciles per i_category, and fit the empirical cs_quantity distribution per (category, band, d_moy). For each cap scenario (candidate caps on a grid), reprice lines above the cap at the cap price, draw quantity from the cap band's distribution, and compute profit = qty*(price - cs_wholesale_cost) - ship_cost_per_unit*qty. Run 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations per scenario. [MISSING_DATA: unconverted quotes or lost orders] limits the demand response to purchased lines. Output schema: (i_category, cap, profit_p10, profit_p50, profit_p90, delta_vs_baseline). As a final step, ai_query recommends a cap per category and explains the risk.

use_cases.Name: Reduce Excess Discounting of Preferred Customers with Discount Targeting Rules
use_cases.Statement: Customers flagged in `c_preferred_cust_flag` may receive deeper `ws_ext_discount_amt` and `ws_coupon_amt` than other customers without buying more `ws_quantity`. If so, the extra discount erodes `ws_net_profit` with no volume return.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `web_sales` to `customer` on `ws_bill_customer_sk` = `c_customer_sk`, to `item` on `ws_item_sk` = `i_item_sk` and to `date_dim` on `ws_sold_date_sk` = `d_date_sk`. Per category, it fits an OLS model of discount depth on preferred status and a Poisson GLM of `ws_quantity` on discount depth interacted with preferred status, which separates extra discount given from extra units earned. The output is a set of discount targeting rules per category: keep, trim or remove the extra discount for preferred customers.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager trims extra discount for preferred customers in categories where it does not raise units. This increases `ws_net_profit` per preferred order and reduces discount dollars from `ws_ext_discount_amt` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_ext_discount_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_quantity, ws_list_price, ws_ext_list_price, ws_ext_discount_amt, ws_coupon_amt, ws_net_profit from web_sales; c_customer_sk, c_preferred_cust_flag from customer; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_moy from date_dim. Approach: (1) Perform the JOINs on the keys listed above and exclude rows with null c_preferred_cust_flag. (2) Compute discount_depth = (ws_ext_discount_amt + ws_coupon_amt)/ws_ext_list_price and preferred = (c_preferred_cust_flag = 'Y'). (3) Model A, OLS per i_category: discount_depth ~ preferred + ws_list_price + d_moy. (4) Model B, Poisson GLM per i_category: ws_quantity ~ discount_depth + preferred + discount_depth*preferred + ws_list_price + d_moy. (5) Derive profit per discount dollar from ws_net_profit by segment. (6) Output: i_category, extra_discount_preferred, unit_response_preferred, unit_response_other, rule (keep, trim or remove). (7) ai_query receives the coefficients per category and writes the targeting rule rationale for the pricing team.

use_cases.Name: Prioritize Loss-Making Web Order Hotspots with Pricing and Fulfillment Fix List
use_cases.Statement: Web orders with negative `ws_net_profit` erode margin. The loss is spread across item, ship mode and site combinations, so no owner sees which few combinations, driven by `ws_ext_discount_amt`, `ws_ext_ship_cost` or below-cost pricing, account for most of it.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `web_sales` to `item` on `ws_item_sk` = `i_item_sk`, to `ship_mode` on `ws_ship_mode_sk` = `sm_ship_mode_sk` and to `web_site` on `ws_web_site_sk` = `web_site_sk`. It tags each losing line with its dominant driver, then ranks class, ship type, carrier and site combinations by cumulative share of total loss. The output is a pricing and fulfillment fix list of the combinations that make up most of the loss, each with its dominant driver and owner.
use_cases.Business Value: The Merchandise Planner fixes the few combinations behind most losses, using price floors, coupon exclusions or carrier changes. This reduces loss-making order count and total negative `ws_net_profit` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_net_profit`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_order_number, ws_item_sk, ws_ship_mode_sk, ws_web_site_sk, ws_net_profit, ws_sales_price, ws_wholesale_cost, ws_ext_discount_amt, ws_coupon_amt, ws_ext_sales_price, ws_ext_ship_cost, ws_net_paid from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_class from item; sm_ship_mode_sk, sm_type, sm_carrier from ship_mode; web_site_sk, web_name from web_site. Approach: (1) Perform the JOINs on the keys listed above. (2) Keep lines with ws_net_profit < 0. (3) Compute driver signals: discount_share = (ws_ext_discount_amt + ws_coupon_amt)/ws_ext_sales_price, below_cost = ws_sales_price < ws_wholesale_cost, ship_ratio = ws_ext_ship_cost/ws_net_paid. Assign each line the dominant driver with the largest standardized signal. (4) Group by i_class, sm_type, sm_carrier and web_name: loss = -SUM(ws_net_profit), orders = COUNT(DISTINCT ws_order_number). (5) Sort by loss and compute cumulative share; keep combinations up to a configurable cumulative cut. (6) Output: combination keys, loss, cumulative_share, dominant_driver, orders. (7) ai_query receives each combination and writes a specific fix (price floor, coupon exclusion or carrier switch) and suggested owner.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Quantity-Break Pricing by Item Class with Volume Price Tier Schedule
use_cases.Statement: Discount depth (`cs_sales_price` relative to `cs_list_price`) currently varies with `cs_quantity` without a deliberate schedule. Large-quantity lines may therefore receive discounts that do not raise units enough to cover the lost `cs_net_profit`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code estimates a quantity-response curve to discount depth for each item class with a log-log regression. It then solves a constrained optimization that picks a discount for each quantity band to maximize expected profit, subject to a margin floor over `cs_wholesale_cost` and monotone tiers, and ai_query explains the tiers. The output is a volume price tier schedule for each item class.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Manager publishes the volume price tier schedule. This should increase `cs_net_profit` per line in high-quantity bands and reduce discount given on lines where it does not raise `cs_quantity` [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_ext_discount_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_item_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_quantity, cs_list_price, cs_sales_price, cs_wholesale_cost, cs_ext_discount_amt, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; i_item_sk, i_class_id, i_class from item; d_date_sk, d_moy from date_dim. Approach: JOIN cs_item_sk = i_item_sk and cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Compute discount = 1 - cs_sales_price / cs_list_price and define quantity bands from cs_quantity quantiles. For each i_class_id, fit OLS of log(cs_quantity) on log(1 - discount) with band and d_moy dummies to obtain band-level response. Optimize the discount per band over a grid of discount levels to maximize the sum over bands of predicted units x (cs_list_price x (1 - discount) - cs_wholesale_cost). Constraints: discount is non-decreasing across bands, and price stays above cs_wholesale_cost times a margin floor set by the Pricing Manager. Output schema: i_class, quantity_band, recommended_discount, expected_units, expected_profit. Final step: ai_query writes the tier rationale and rollout notes.

use_cases.Name: Detect Shelf Price Errors at Stores with Price Correction Queue
use_cases.Statement: Store sale lines can ring up at a `ss_list_price` that differs from the item master `i_current_price` for the same `i_item_sk` version. Persistent gaps at one store either give away margin or overcharge shoppers, and they go unnoticed because no one reconciles ticket prices to the master record.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `store_sales` to `item` on `ss_item_sk` = `i_item_sk` and builds store-item-week features from the gap between `ss_list_price` and `i_current_price`, the gap's persistence, the share of affected lines and the `ss_sales_price` to `ss_list_price` ratio. An Isolation Forest scores each store-item-week, and ai_query writes a correction note for each flagged case, producing a daily price correction queue for store pricing teams.
use_cases.Business Value: The Pricing Operations Manager corrects the highest-exposure store price records each week, reducing undercharged revenue computed as `ss_quantity` x (`i_current_price` - `ss_list_price`) [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_list_price` and `i_current_price`]. The same queue also reduces overcharged lines that create customer complaints.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_list_price, ss_sales_price, ss_quantity, ss_promo_sk from store_sales; i_item_sk, i_current_price, i_rec_start_date, i_rec_end_date, i_category from item; s_store_sk, s_store_name from store; d_date_sk, d_date, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: JOIN store_sales ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk, ON ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Keep lines where d_date falls between i_rec_start_date and i_rec_end_date. Aggregate to store-item-week and compute these features: gap_ratio = avg(ss_list_price - i_current_price)/i_current_price; persistence = count of consecutive d_week_seq with nonzero gap; affected_line_share; promo_null_share (ss_promo_sk null); and sale_to_list = avg(ss_sales_price/ss_list_price). Train an Isolation Forest (contamination=0.02, n_estimators=200) within each i_category. Output columns: store, item, week, gap_ratio, exposure = sum(ss_quantity*(i_current_price - ss_list_price)), and anomaly_score. ai_query then explains each flagged row and recommends correcting the store price record or escalating a master data error.

use_cases.Name: Simulate Promotion Funding Scenarios with Promotion Budget Reallocation Plan
use_cases.Statement: Promotions carry a `p_cost` and target `p_response_target`, but the incremental `ss_net_profit`, `cs_net_profit` and `ws_net_profit` they generate on the promoted `p_item_sk` is uncertain. Budget is renewed without comparing channel mixes.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code estimates incremental profit per promotion against baseline weeks for the promoted item. It bootstraps lift distributions by channel mix (`p_channel_dmail`, `p_channel_email`, `p_channel_tv`) and runs Monte Carlo budget scenarios. The output is a promotion budget reallocation plan with keep and cut decisions.
use_cases.Business Value: The Promotions Manager moves budget from promotions whose simulated profit net of `p_cost` is likely negative. This increases total incremental net profit per promotion dollar [ESTIMATE: depends on `p_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: p_promo_sk, p_start_date_sk, p_end_date_sk, p_item_sk, p_cost, p_response_target, p_channel_dmail, p_channel_email, p_channel_tv, p_discount_active from promotion; ss_promo_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_net_profit from store_sales; cs_promo_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; ws_promo_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_net_profit from web_sales; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: (1) JOIN sales to promotion ON ss_promo_sk = p_promo_sk (and the cs and ws equivalents), with the promo-sk join inferred from column naming. (2) JOIN date_dim ON p_start_date_sk / p_end_date_sk = d_date_sk to get the promo window in d_week_seq. (3) Compute promo-window weekly net profit for p_item_sk versus baseline = mean weekly net profit for the same item in non-promo weeks, giving lift = promo minus baseline. (4) Group promotions by channel-mix signature (dmail, email, tv flags plus p_discount_active). (5) Monte Carlo with 10,000 draws: bootstrap lift per signature, then for each scenario (current allocation and shifted allocations) simulate total net return = SUM(lift) - SUM(p_cost). Output: scenario, expected_net_return, p10, p90, probability_negative, plus a per-promotion keep/cut flag. Final step: ai_query writes the reallocation plan, explaining which channel mixes to fund and which to retire.

use_cases.Name: Simulate Coupon Cap Policies with Promotion Guardrail Recommendations
use_cases.Statement: Coupons recorded in `ws_coupon_amt` reduce `ws_net_paid` and `ws_net_profit`. There is no way to see how capping coupons per category would trade lost units against recovered profit, or how uncertain that trade-off is.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code estimates bootstrapped unit-response distributions to coupon depth per `i_category`. It then runs Monte Carlo scenarios that cap `ws_coupon_amt` as a share of `ws_ext_list_price`. The output is a set of promotion guardrail recommendations listing, per category, the cap with the highest probability of a profit gain.
use_cases.Business Value: The Revenue Management Lead sets coupon caps per category from simulated profit distributions instead of trial and error. This increases `ws_net_profit` and reduces `ws_coupon_amt` spend [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_coupon_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_item_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_quantity, ws_coupon_amt, ws_ext_list_price, ws_ext_sales_price, ws_ext_wholesale_cost, ws_net_paid, ws_net_profit from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Joins: JOIN item ON ws_item_sk = i_item_sk; JOIN date_dim ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Per i_category, fit a log-log regression of weekly units on coupon depth (sum ws_coupon_amt / sum ws_ext_list_price) and bootstrap 500 coefficient draws. Monte Carlo with 10,000 draws per scenario and cap level: (a) apply the cap to each historical line; (b) adjust units by the sampled response; (c) recompute net profit = ws_ext_sales_price - ws_coupon_amt - ws_ext_wholesale_cost on the scaled units. Output: i_category, cap level, P10, P50 and P90 profit change, probability of gain. Final step: ai_query recommends a guardrail per category and states the downside risk.

use_cases.Name: Identify Unprofitable Coupon-Acquired Cohorts with Acquisition Incentive Policy
use_cases.Statement: Customers whose first order carried `ws_coupon_amt` or deep `ws_ext_discount_amt` may never earn back that incentive in later `ws_net_profit`. There is currently no cohort view showing which acquisition incentives actually pay back.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code forms acquisition cohorts from each customer's first-order month on `d_month_seq`, coupon use and discount band. It then tracks cumulative `ws_net_profit` and repeat orders by month since acquisition. The output is an acquisition incentive policy table giving each cohort's payback month and a keep, cap or stop decision.
use_cases.Business Value: The Promotions Manager caps or stops first-order incentives for cohorts that never reach payback on `ws_net_profit`. This increases cumulative profit per acquired customer and reduces acquisition coupon spend in `ws_coupon_amt` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_coupon_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_bill_customer_sk, ws_order_number, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_coupon_amt, ws_ext_discount_amt, ws_ext_list_price, ws_net_profit from web_sales; d_date_sk, d_month_seq from date_dim. Join: JOIN date_dim ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Per customer: cohort_month = MIN(d_month_seq); first-order coupon flag; first-order discount band from ws_ext_discount_amt / ws_ext_list_price (cut at tertiles). For each later order, month_offset = d_month_seq - cohort_month. Build a cohort x month_offset matrix of cumulative ws_net_profit per customer and repeat-order rate. Compare cohort curves with bootstrap confidence intervals (500 resamples) and compute each cohort's payback month. Output: cohort_month, coupon_flag, discount_band, payback_month, cumulative profit at month 12, policy action. Final step: ai_query recommends the incentive policy per cohort and explains the evidence.

use_cases.Name: Segment Items by Weekly Demand Rhythm with Promotion Timing Calendar
use_cases.Statement: Items differ in when they sell: their share of `ss_quantity` by `d_dow`, `t_hour` and `d_moy` varies. Yet promotions flagged by `ss_promo_sk` are scheduled without regard to these demand rhythms, so promoted weeks may miss each item's natural peaks.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds normalized demand-shape vectors per `i_item_id` from `ss_quantity` by day of week, hour band and month. It clusters the vectors with K-Means and compares promoted-unit lift when promotion timing matched the cluster peak versus when it did not. It delivers a promotion timing calendar per demand-rhythm cluster.
use_cases.Business Value: The Promotion Planner schedules promotions in each cluster's peak windows. This increases promoted `ss_quantity` and `ss_net_profit` per promoted item-week, measurable against off-peak promotions [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_quantity`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_sold_time_sk, ss_quantity, ss_promo_sk, ss_net_profit from store_sales; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_dow, d_moy, d_week_seq from date_dim; t_time_sk, t_hour from time_dim. Joins: ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk, ss_sold_time_sk = t_time_sk. Per i_item_id with sufficient unit volume, build a 23-dimensional shape vector: 7 d_dow shares, 4 t_hour band shares and 12 d_moy shares, each normalized to sum to 1. Run K-Means (k-means++, k from 4 to 10 selected by silhouette) and identify each cluster's peak dow and month windows. Compute promoted lift = promoted-week units divided by the same item's non-promoted baseline, split by whether the promotion week fell in the peak window, and test the difference with Mann-Whitney U. Output: i_item_id, i_category, cluster_id, peak_dow, peak_months, aligned_lift, misaligned_lift, p_value. ai_query names each cluster and writes the promotion timing calendar.

use_cases.Name: Simulate Promotion Discount Scenarios with Category Promotion Budget Guardrails
use_cases.Statement: Promoted lines (non-null `ss_promo_sk`) carry deeper `ss_ext_discount_amt`. Planners do not know the range of `ss_net_profit` outcomes a given discount depth could produce in each `i_category` once volume uncertainty is taken into account.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code bootstraps the observed unit lift of promoted versus non-promoted item-weeks per `i_category` from `ss_quantity` and margins from `ss_wholesale_cost`. It runs a Monte Carlo simulation across a grid of discount depths and delivers promotion budget guardrails: the maximum discount depth per category whose simulated chance of a profit decline stays below the planner's tolerance.
use_cases.Business Value: The Promotion Planner approves discount depths within the simulated guardrails. This reduces the count of promoted item-weeks with negative incremental `ss_net_profit` and the `ss_ext_discount_amt` spent on them [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_net_profit`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_promo_sk, ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_sales_price, ss_wholesale_cost, ss_ext_discount_amt, ss_net_profit from store_sales; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Joins: ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Build item-week records with units, promo flag (any non-null ss_promo_sk), average discount depth = 1 - ss_sales_price/ss_list_price, and unit margin from ss_wholesale_cost. Per i_category, estimate the distribution of unit lift versus same-item non-promo weeks with 1000 bootstrap resamples. Monte Carlo: 10,000 draws per scenario over a discount-depth grid spanning the observed range, sampling lift and baseline units. Profit = units x (list x (1 - depth) - wholesale). Report P5, P50 and P95 incremental profit and P(incremental profit < 0). Output: i_category, discount_depth, p5_profit, p50_profit, p95_profit, prob_loss, guardrail_flag. ai_query writes a guardrail memo per category explaining the tradeoffs.

use_cases.Name: Prioritize Web Promotions by Incremental Profit with Promotion Renewal Shortlist
use_cases.Statement: Promotions identified by `ws_promo_sk` are renewed without evidence that the units they sell at reduced `ws_sales_price` add `ws_net_profit` beyond what the same items earn in comparable non-promoted weeks.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `web_sales` to `item` on `ws_item_sk` = `i_item_sk` and to `date_dim` on `ws_sold_date_sk` = `d_date_sk`. It fits a per-category Ridge regression of item-week `ws_net_profit` on promotion indicators from `ws_promo_sk`, item fixed effects and calendar controls, giving each promotion an incremental profit estimate with a bootstrap interval. Promotion attributes beyond the id are not available [MISSING_DATA: promotion attributes such as cost and channel]. The output is a promotion renewal shortlist that labels each promotion Renew, Rework or Retire.
use_cases.Business Value: The Promotions Manager renews only promotions with a positive incremental profit interval and retires those with a negative one. This increases net profit per promoted unit, measured from `ws_net_profit` and `ws_quantity` [ESTIMATE: depends on `ws_net_profit`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ws_promo_sk, ws_item_sk, ws_sold_date_sk, ws_quantity, ws_sales_price, ws_list_price, ws_net_profit, ws_ext_discount_amt from web_sales; i_item_sk, i_category, i_class from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_moy, d_holiday from date_dim. Approach: (1) JOIN ON ws_item_sk = i_item_sk and ON ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Aggregate per item-week (d_week_seq): units = SUM(ws_quantity), profit = SUM(ws_net_profit), price_ratio = AVG(ws_sales_price/ws_list_price). (3) Create one-hot indicators per ws_promo_sk; a null ws_promo_sk means no promotion. (4) Fit Ridge regression (alpha=1.0) per i_category: profit ~ promo dummies + item fixed effects + d_moy + holiday-week flag from d_holiday. (5) Bootstrap 200 resamples for confidence intervals. (6) Output: ws_promo_sk, i_category, incremental_profit_per_week, ci_low, ci_high, items_covered, decision (Renew if ci_low > 0, Retire if ci_high < 0, otherwise Rework). (7) ai_query receives each promotion's coefficients and price_ratio and writes a renewal rationale and rework suggestion.

use_cases.Name: Prioritize Catalog Promotions by Incremental Profit with Promotion Renewal Decision List
use_cases.Statement: Catalog lines carry a promotion identifier `cs_promo_sk`. Nobody measures whether each promotion lifts `cs_quantity` and `cs_net_profit` by more than the value it gives away in `cs_ext_discount_amt` and `cs_coupon_amt`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds weekly item-class panels with promotion exposure shares. It fits a fixed-effects regression of units and profit on exposure to each promotion, and ai_query writes a renewal rationale for each promotion. The output is a promotion renewal decision list labelling each promotion renew, rework or retire.
use_cases.Business Value: The Promotions Manager renews or retires catalog promotions from the list. This should increase `cs_net_profit` per promoted unit and reduce `cs_ext_discount_amt` spent on promotions that do not lift sales [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_ext_discount_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_promo_sk, cs_item_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_quantity, cs_ext_discount_amt, cs_coupon_amt, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; i_item_sk, i_class_id, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_moy, d_holiday from date_dim. Approach: JOIN cs_item_sk = i_item_sk and cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Build a panel per i_class_id x d_week_seq with units = SUM(cs_quantity), profit = SUM(cs_net_profit), giveaway = SUM(cs_ext_discount_amt + cs_coupon_amt), and an exposure share for each of the top-N cs_promo_sk (units on that promotion divided by total units). Fit a Ridge model (alpha=0.5) with fixed effects for i_class_id and d_moy and a holiday-week flag from d_holiday. Run separate models for units and profit, and bootstrap confidence intervals with 200 resamples. Promotions with a profit coefficient significantly below zero are labelled retire, and those with positive units but negative profit are labelled rework. [MISSING_DATA: promotion attributes and spend, the promotion table is not in scope]. Output schema: cs_promo_sk, units_lift_coef, profit_lift_coef, ci_low, ci_high, decision. Final step: ai_query explains each decision.

use_cases.Name: Optimize Discount Generosity for Preferred Shoppers with Benefit Recalibration Plan
use_cases.Statement: Shoppers with `c_preferred_cust_flag` = Y receive discounts (`ss_ext_discount_amt`) and coupons (`ss_coupon_amt`). Nobody knows whether that generosity produces incremental `ss_net_profit` or simply subsidizes spend that would have happened anyway, and the answer may differ by category.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `store_sales` to `customer` and `item` and builds customer-quarter spend, trip, discount and coupon features. It estimates the propensity of `c_preferred_cust_flag` = Y with logistic regression, then fits an inverse-propensity-weighted Ridge regression of quarterly `ss_net_profit` on the flag interacted with `i_category`. ai_query turns the category-level effects into a benefit recalibration plan stating where to deepen, hold or trim discounts for preferred shoppers.
use_cases.Business Value: The CRM Manager resets discount depth for preferred shoppers category by category. The goal is to increase net profit per preferred customer, measured from `ss_net_profit`, while reducing discount and coupon cost from `ss_ext_discount_amt` and `ss_coupon_amt` in categories that show no lift [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_ext_discount_amt`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_customer_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_ticket_number, ss_net_paid, ss_net_profit, ss_ext_discount_amt, ss_coupon_amt from store_sales; c_customer_sk, c_preferred_cust_flag, c_birth_year, c_first_sales_date_sk from customer; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_quarter_seq, d_year from date_dim. Approach: JOIN ON ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk, ss_item_sk = i_item_sk and ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Build customer x category x d_quarter_seq features: net_paid, net_profit, discount_amt, coupon_amt, trips = count distinct ss_ticket_number, prior_quarter_net_paid, tenure in quarters since c_first_sales_date_sk, and age = d_year - c_birth_year. Estimate the propensity of preferred status with logistic regression on the pre-treatment covariates and trim weights at the 1st and 99th percentiles. Fit a weighted Ridge regression (alpha=1.0) of net_profit on flag x i_category plus covariates. Output columns: category, preferred_effect_on_profit, discount_per_preferred_customer and recommended_action. ai_query then explains each category effect and drafts the recalibration plan.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Weekly Return Losses by Category with Refund Reserve Plan
use_cases.Statement: Finance has no forward view of the `cr_net_loss` and `cr_return_amt_inc_tax` that catalog returns will generate in coming weeks for each `i_category`. Refund reserves are therefore set reactively and can fall short in peak return weeks.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates `cr_net_loss` and `cr_return_amt_inc_tax` weekly by `i_category` using `d_week_seq`. It fits per-category forecasts that use holiday flags from `d_holiday`, and its final output is a weekly refund reserve plan per category with upper-bound loss intervals.
use_cases.Business Value: The Finance Planning Manager sets weekly refund reserves per category from the forecast instead of trailing averages. This reduces reserve shortfall, measured as actual minus reserved `cr_net_loss` per `i_category` [ESTIMATE: depends on cr_net_loss].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cr_returned_date_sk, cr_item_sk, cr_net_loss, cr_return_amt_inc_tax, cr_return_quantity from catalog_returns; i_item_sk, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_year, d_moy, d_holiday, d_following_holiday from date_dim. JOIN item ON cr_item_sk = i_item_sk and JOIN date_dim ON cr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk (inferred surrogate date join). Aggregate weekly SUM(cr_net_loss), SUM(cr_return_amt_inc_tax) and SUM(cr_return_quantity) per i_category. Add holiday-day counts per week from d_holiday and d_following_holiday as regressors, then fit Prophet per category (yearly seasonality on, changepoint_prior_scale=0.05, 80 and 95 percent intervals). Backtest on the last 13 weeks with MAPE. Output schema: i_category, d_week_seq, forecast_net_loss, p95_net_loss, recommended_reserve. Final step: ai_query receives the forecasts and backtest error, explains the drivers of each category's trajectory and recommends reserve adjustments in plain language.

use_cases.Name: Simulate Store Credit Settlement Shifts with Refund Policy Recommendation
use_cases.Statement: Catalog returns are settled through a mix of `cr_refunded_cash`, `cr_reversed_charge` and `cr_store_credit`. Treasury cannot see the range of monthly cash outflow if the store credit share changes for specific `r_reason_desc` and `i_category` combinations.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code bootstraps monthly return value and settlement shares by reason and category, then runs a Monte Carlo simulation of settlement-mix scenarios. The output is a refund policy recommendation that names the reason and category cells where shifting toward `cr_store_credit` most reduces P95 cash outflow.
use_cases.Business Value: The Treasury Manager selects the reason and category cells for settlement policy changes using simulated cash-outflow ranges. This reduces P95 monthly cash refunded via `cr_refunded_cash` plus `cr_reversed_charge` [ESTIMATE: depends on cr_refunded_cash].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cr_item_sk, cr_reason_sk, cr_returned_date_sk, cr_return_amt_inc_tax, cr_refunded_cash, cr_reversed_charge, cr_store_credit from catalog_returns; i_item_sk, i_category from item; r_reason_sk, r_reason_desc from reason; d_date_sk, d_month_seq, d_moy from date_dim. JOIN item ON cr_item_sk = i_item_sk, JOIN reason ON cr_reason_sk = r_reason_sk and JOIN date_dim ON cr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk (inferred). Per i_category, r_reason_desc and d_month_seq, compute total cr_return_amt_inc_tax and the cash, reversed and credit shares. Run a Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations that bootstraps monthly totals conditioned on d_moy. For each scenario, shift the credit share up by a configurable amount (for example 0, 5 or 10 points) for selected cells, reallocating proportionally from cash and reversed charge. Compute the P50 and P95 monthly cash outflow, defined as cash plus reversed charge. Output schema: scenario_id, i_category, r_reason_desc, p50_cash_outflow, p95_cash_outflow, delta_vs_baseline. Final step: ai_query compares the scenarios and recommends which cells to target, noting customer-experience caveats.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Refund Liability by Product Category with Refund Reserve Plan
use_cases.Statement: Finance reserves for web refunds without a forward view of `wr_return_amt_inc_tax` and `wr_net_loss`, so swings in returns by `i_category` cause cash and accrual surprises. A daily-key forecast lets reserves and reverse-logistics capacity track expected returns.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates `wr_return_amt_inc_tax`, `wr_net_loss` and `wr_return_quantity` per `wr_returned_date_sk` and `i_category`, then fits Prophet models per category with weekly seasonality. The output is a refund reserve plan with forecast intervals per category and an ai_query narrative recommending reserve and capacity levels.
use_cases.Business Value: The FP&A Manager sets the monthly refund reserve and reverse-logistics staffing from the forecast, reducing the gap between reserved and actual `wr_return_amt_inc_tax` [ESTIMATE: depends on wr_return_amt_inc_tax]. Forecast error against realized refunds is tracked monthly to prove accuracy gains.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: wr_returned_date_sk, wr_return_amt_inc_tax, wr_net_loss, wr_return_quantity, wr_item_sk from web_returns joined with i_item_sk, i_category from item ON wr_item_sk = i_item_sk. Treat wr_returned_date_sk as a consecutive ordinal day key and derive day-of-week as MOD(wr_returned_date_sk,7) [MISSING_DATA: date_dim calendar table for true dates and holidays]. Aggregate daily totals per i_category, fill missing days with zero, fit Prophet (weekly seasonality on, changepoint_prior_scale=0.05) per category, backtest with rolling-origin cross-validation, forecast 90 days with 80 percent intervals. Output: category, day key, forecast, lower, upper. Final step: ai_query explains forecast drivers and recommends reserve and staffing levels per category.

use_cases.Name: Simulate Working Capital Tied in Inventory with Quarterly Budget Plan
use_cases.Statement: Finance has no range estimate of next-quarter capital tied in stock, valued as `inv_quantity_on_hand` times `i_wholesale_cost` across `w_warehouse_name`. Working-capital budgets are therefore set without any view of downside or upside exposure.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code runs a Monte Carlo simulation that bootstraps historical snapshot-over-snapshot changes in `inv_quantity_on_hand` per category and warehouse. Each simulated path is valued at `i_wholesale_cost`, which produces P10, P50 and P90 capital paths for the next quarter. The output is a quarterly budget plan with purchase caps for each warehouse.
use_cases.Business Value: The FP&A Manager sets working-capital budgets and purchase caps from the simulated P50 and P90 instead of a single point estimate. The target is to reduce variance between budgeted and realized capital at cost computed from `inv_quantity_on_hand` and `i_wholesale_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on i_wholesale_cost].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: inv_date_sk, inv_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk, inv_quantity_on_hand from inventory; i_item_sk, i_category, i_wholesale_cost from item; w_warehouse_sk, w_warehouse_name from warehouse; d_date_sk, d_week_seq, d_qoy from date_dim. Approach: (1) Join ON inv_item_sk = i_item_sk, inv_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk and inv_date_sk = d_date_sk. (2) Per i_category and w_warehouse_name, compute the weekly capital at cost and its snapshot-over-snapshot changes. Stratify the changes by d_qoy to keep seasonality. (3) Run 10,000 Monte Carlo paths over the next 13 snapshots using a block bootstrap (block length = 4) of the historical changes from the matching quarter, starting from the latest capital. Floor capital at zero. (4) Output columns: warehouse, category, P10, P50 and P90 end-of-quarter capital, plus the probability of exceeding the current budget line, which is an input parameter. (5) ai_query writes the budget plan narrative and recommended purchase caps for each warehouse.

use_cases.Name: Predict Return Tail After Catalog Pages Expire with Reserve Release Schedule
use_cases.Statement: Returns keep arriving after a catalog page's active window closes at `cp_end_date_sk`, so finance holds return reserves for expired editions without knowing when the tail of `cr_net_loss` has run out. Releasing too early understates liability, and releasing too late ties up cash.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code computes, for every return, the days from page start `cp_start_date_sk` to `cr_returned_date_sk`, fits Kaplan-Meier curves by `cp_type` and a Cox model with item category and `cr_return_amount` covariates, and derives when the remaining expected return value per page type falls below a finance-set threshold. The output is a reserve release schedule per catalog page type and category.
use_cases.Business Value: The Financial Planning Manager releases expired-edition return reserves on the schedule, freeing cash earlier while keeping the gap between reserved and realized `cr_net_loss` small [ESTIMATE: depends on `cr_net_loss`]. Late-arriving `cr_return_amount` after the release date is tracked as the accuracy KPI.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cr_returned_date_sk, cr_catalog_page_sk, cr_item_sk, cr_return_amount, cr_net_loss from catalog_returns; cp_catalog_page_sk, cp_start_date_sk, cp_end_date_sk, cp_type, cp_catalog_number from catalog_page; d_date_sk, d_date from date_dim; i_item_sk, i_category from item. JOIN catalog_page ON cr_catalog_page_sk = cp_catalog_page_sk; JOIN date_dim dr ON cr_returned_date_sk = dr.d_date_sk, ds ON cp_start_date_sk = ds.d_date_sk, de ON cp_end_date_sk = de.d_date_sk (date joins inferred from key naming); JOIN item ON cr_item_sk = i_item_sk. Duration = DATEDIFF(dr.d_date, ds.d_date); post_end_flag = dr.d_date > de.d_date; censor pages whose window ends near the latest observed return date. Fit Kaplan-Meier by cp_type and Cox PH (penalizer=0.1) with i_category, cr_return_amount and window length (de minus ds) as covariates; weight curves by cr_net_loss to get a value-based tail. Output schema: cp_type, i_category, days_after_end, remaining_expected_net_loss_share, recommended_release_day. Return curves only cover returned items [MISSING_DATA: catalog sales per page for return-rate exposure]. Pass the curves to ai_query to explain the tail shape and recommend release timing per page type.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Weekly Coupon Redemption Cost by Store with Accrual Plan
use_cases.Statement: Weekly coupon cost in `ss_coupon_amt` swings by store and around `d_holiday` periods. Finance accrues it after the fact, which causes promotion budget overruns and late corrections against `ss_net_profit`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `store_sales` to `date_dim` and `store` to build a weekly coupon cost series per store. It fits Prophet with holiday and weekend regressors to forecast 13 weeks ahead with prediction intervals, and ai_query writes a store-level accrual plan with P50 and P90 amounts and drivers.
use_cases.Business Value: The Promotions Finance Analyst books coupon accruals from the forecast instead of after redemption. This reduces the gap between accrued and actual `ss_coupon_amt` and prevents budget overruns [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_coupon_amt`]. [MISSING_DATA: planned coupon campaign calendar].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_coupon_amt, ss_ext_sales_price, ss_ticket_number from store_sales; d_date_sk, d_date, d_week_seq, d_holiday, d_weekend, d_following_holiday from date_dim; s_store_sk, s_store_name from store. Approach: JOIN ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and ss_store_sk = s_store_sk. Aggregate weekly per store: coupon_cost = sum(ss_coupon_amt), coupon_tickets = count distinct ss_ticket_number with coupon > 0, and sales = sum(ss_ext_sales_price). Add regressors for weekly holiday count from d_holiday and d_following_holiday. Fit Prophet per store with yearly seasonality and holiday regressors, interval_width=0.9, horizon 13 weeks, and run rolling-origin backtests reporting MAPE. Output columns: store, week, p50, p90 and coupon_share_of_sales. ai_query then explains the forecast drivers and drafts the accrual plan.

use_cases.Name: Forecast Store Credit Issuance by Store with Credit Liability Reserve Plan
use_cases.Statement: Store credit issued on returns (`sr_store_credit`) is an outstanding obligation that varies by store (`s_store_sk`) and by week. Without a forward view, finance cannot reserve for it accurately.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code aggregates `sr_store_credit` weekly by store using `sr_returned_date_sk` as the time axis and fits a forecast per store with prediction intervals. The output is a credit liability reserve plan with recommended weekly reserve levels per store.
use_cases.Business Value: The Treasury Analyst sets weekly store credit reserves from the forecast bands. The goal is to reduce the gap between reserved amounts and actual `sr_store_credit` issued [ESTIMATE: depends on `sr_store_credit`]. Impact is measured by backtesting forecast error against the current reserving approach.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: sr_returned_date_sk, sr_store_sk, sr_store_credit, sr_return_amt_inc_tax, sr_refunded_cash from store_returns; s_store_sk, s_store_name, s_market_id from store. Approach: (1) JOIN store ON sr_store_sk = s_store_sk. (2) Build a week index = FLOOR(sr_returned_date_sk/7) [ASSUMPTION: date keys are sequential day numbers; MISSING_DATA: date_dim for holiday and calendar effects]. (3) Aggregate weekly SUM(sr_store_credit) and the credit share of sr_return_amt_inc_tax per s_store_sk. (4) Fit Prophet per store with yearly_seasonality approximated by a 52-week Fourier order of 5 and changepoint_prior_scale=0.05. Validate with a rolling-origin backtest on 13-week holdouts. (5) Output schema: s_store_name, week_index, forecast, lower_80, upper_80, recommended_reserve = upper_80. (6) ai_query explains store-level drivers and recommends reserve adjustments, producing the credit liability reserve plan.

use_cases.Name: Predict Next-Quarter Return Losses by Item with Assortment Review Queue
use_cases.Statement: Assortment reviews look backward and do not anticipate which items, identified by `i_item_id`, will generate the largest `cr_net_loss` next quarter. Signals such as rising reason shares in `r_reason_desc` and margin from `i_current_price` versus `i_wholesale_cost` go unused.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code builds an item-by-quarter panel of lagged `cr_net_loss`, return counts, reason shares and price attributes, then trains a LightGBM model to predict next-quarter item loss. The output is an assortment review queue ranked by predicted loss, with SHAP drivers for each item.
use_cases.Business Value: The Assortment Planner reviews, re-describes or delists the items with the highest predicted return loss before the quarter starts. This reduces next-quarter `cr_net_loss` for reviewed items [ESTIMATE: depends on cr_net_loss].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cr_item_sk, cr_reason_sk, cr_returned_date_sk, cr_order_number, cr_return_quantity, cr_net_loss from catalog_returns; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost, i_category, i_brand_id, i_manufact_id from item; r_reason_sk, r_reason_desc from reason; d_date_sk, d_quarter_seq from date_dim. JOIN item ON cr_item_sk = i_item_sk, JOIN reason ON cr_reason_sk = r_reason_sk and JOIN date_dim ON cr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk (inferred). Build a panel per i_item_id and d_quarter_seq. Features: lag-1 to lag-4 SUM(cr_net_loss) and COUNT(DISTINCT cr_order_number), quarter-over-quarter growth, the share of returns for each of the top 6 r_reason_desc values, i_current_price, the margin i_current_price - i_wholesale_cost, and one-hot i_category, i_brand_id and i_manufact_id. The target is next-quarter SUM(cr_net_loss). Train LightGBM (num_leaves=31, learning_rate=0.05, 500 rounds with early stopping) using rolling-origin time cross-validation, and report MAE versus a naive lag-1 baseline. Item sales volume is not available [MISSING_DATA: catalog sales by item], so the predicted loss is absolute rather than a rate. Output schema: i_item_id, predicted_net_loss, rank, top_shap_drivers. Final step: ai_query explains each top-ranked item's drivers and recommends a review action.

use_cases.Name: Detect Sales Tax Collection Errors on Catalog Orders with Tax Correction Queue
use_cases.Statement: The effective tax rate on a line (`cs_ext_tax` divided by `cs_ext_sales_price`) should be consistent across lines taken by the same call center and close to its `cc_tax_percentage`. Lines that deviate create exposure from under-collected or over-collected tax.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code computes the effective rate, the gap to `cc_tax_percentage`, peer deviation and a check of `cs_net_paid_inc_tax` minus `cs_net_paid` against `cs_ext_tax`. It trains an Isolation Forest per call center, and ai_query summarizes the likely cause for each flagged group. The output is a tax correction queue of flagged order lines, ranked by tax amount at risk, for the tax team to review.
use_cases.Business Value: The Tax Compliance Manager works the queue weekly. This should reduce the value of mis-collected `cs_ext_tax` and the count of orders that need later amendment [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_ext_tax`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_order_number, cs_item_sk, cs_call_center_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_quantity, cs_ext_sales_price, cs_ext_tax, cs_net_paid, cs_net_paid_inc_tax from catalog_sales; cc_call_center_sk, cc_name, cc_state, cc_tax_percentage from call_center; d_date_sk, d_month_seq from date_dim. Approach: JOIN cs_call_center_sk = cc_call_center_sk and cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Features: eff_rate = cs_ext_tax / NULLIF(cs_ext_sales_price,0); gap_center = eff_rate - cc_tax_percentage; peer_dev = eff_rate minus the median eff_rate within cc_call_center_sk x d_month_seq; recon_gap = (cs_net_paid_inc_tax - cs_net_paid) - cs_ext_tax; log cs_ext_sales_price; cs_quantity. Train Isolation Forest (n_estimators=200, contamination=0.01) per cc_call_center_sk. Compute tax_at_risk = ABS(cs_ext_tax - cc_tax_percentage * cs_ext_sales_price). [MISSING_DATA: ship-to jurisdiction tax rates] would sharpen the expected rate. Output schema: cs_order_number, cs_item_sk, cc_name, eff_rate, anomaly_score, tax_at_risk. Final step: ai_query explains the flagged groups and recommends a correction action for each.

use_cases.Name: Detect Misrecorded Wholesale Costs on Catalog Orders with Cost Correction Queue
use_cases.Statement: The line cost `cs_wholesale_cost` should agree with the item record's `i_wholesale_cost` for the version valid on the sale date. Unexplained divergence misstates `cs_net_profit`, which pricing and assortment decisions rely on.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins each line to its item version and checks validity against `i_rec_start_date` and `i_rec_end_date`. It builds cost-ratio and consistency features, trains an Isolation Forest per category, and ai_query explains each flagged pattern. The output is a cost correction queue ranked by profit misstatement for the cost accounting team to resolve.
use_cases.Business Value: The Cost Accountant corrects the flagged cost records. This should reduce misstated `cs_net_profit` value and the count of lines with inconsistent `cs_ext_wholesale_cost` [ESTIMATE: depends on `cs_wholesale_cost`].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: cs_order_number, cs_item_sk, cs_sold_date_sk, cs_quantity, cs_wholesale_cost, cs_ext_wholesale_cost, cs_list_price, cs_net_profit from catalog_sales; i_item_sk, i_item_id, i_wholesale_cost, i_rec_start_date, i_rec_end_date, i_brand_id, i_category from item; d_date_sk, d_date, d_month_seq from date_dim. Approach: JOIN cs_item_sk = i_item_sk and cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Features: cost_ratio = cs_wholesale_cost / i_wholesale_cost; version_valid = d_date BETWEEN i_rec_start_date AND COALESCE(i_rec_end_date, d_date); ext_gap = cs_ext_wholesale_cost - cs_wholesale_cost * cs_quantity; markup = cs_list_price / cs_wholesale_cost; peer_dev = cost_ratio minus the median within i_brand_id x d_month_seq. Train Isolation Forest (n_estimators=200, contamination=0.02) per i_category. Compute misstatement = (cs_wholesale_cost - i_wholesale_cost) * cs_quantity. Output schema: cs_order_number, i_item_id, cost_ratio, version_valid, anomaly_score, misstatement. Final step: ai_query diagnoses whether each cluster looks like a stale version, an entry error or an extension error and recommends the fix.

use_cases.Name: Detect Supplier Unit Cost Overcharges with Cost Recovery Audit Queue
use_cases.Statement: The unit cost recorded on store sales, `ss_wholesale_cost`, can drift above the item master `i_wholesale_cost` for specific manufacturers and stores. That drift inflates `ss_ext_wholesale_cost` and erodes `ss_net_profit` without any explicit cost change being approved.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code joins `store_sales` to `item` on `ss_item_sk` = `i_item_sk` and aggregates cost-gap features by `i_manufact_id`, `ss_store_sk` and week. These features include the gap between `ss_wholesale_cost` and `i_wholesale_cost`, its dispersion across stores and its weekly trend. An Isolation Forest flags abnormal manufacturer-store-weeks, and ai_query drafts a supplier dispute summary for each one, producing a ranked cost recovery audit queue.
use_cases.Business Value: The Procurement Cost Analyst raises cost disputes with the manufacturers at the top of the queue, recovering overpaid cost computed as `ss_quantity` x (`ss_wholesale_cost` - `i_wholesale_cost`) [ESTIMATE: depends on `ss_wholesale_cost` and `i_wholesale_cost`]. Over time this increases recorded `ss_net_profit`.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: ss_item_sk, ss_store_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_quantity, ss_wholesale_cost, ss_ext_wholesale_cost, ss_net_profit from store_sales; i_item_sk, i_wholesale_cost, i_manufact_id, i_manufact, i_class from item; d_date_sk, d_week_seq from date_dim. Approach: JOIN store_sales ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk and ON ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk. Aggregate to i_manufact_id x ss_store_sk x d_week_seq and compute these features: cost_gap_ratio = avg((ss_wholesale_cost - i_wholesale_cost)/i_wholesale_cost); cross_store_dispersion = stddev of the gap across stores for the same manufacturer-week; gap_slope over the trailing 8 weeks; and overpaid_amount = sum(greatest(ss_wholesale_cost - i_wholesale_cost,0)*ss_quantity). Train an Isolation Forest (contamination=0.03). Output columns: manufacturer, store, week, overpaid_amount, anomaly_score and rank. ai_query then summarizes each flagged case and recommends a dispute or a master cost update.

use_cases.Name: Detect Over-Refunded Tax and Settlement Mismatches with Refund Correction Queue
use_cases.Statement: Return lines can refund more tax than the store's `s_tax_precentage` implies. A line can also split `sr_refunded_cash`, `sr_reversed_charge` and `sr_store_credit` so that the parts do not reconcile to `sr_return_amt_inc_tax`. Either case creates tax filing exposure and cash leakage.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code computes, for each return line, the gap between the implied tax rate (`sr_return_tax` / `sr_return_amt`) and the store `s_tax_precentage`, along with settlement reconciliation gaps. An Isolation Forest scores these features, and the output is a refund correction queue of suspect lines grouped by store.
use_cases.Business Value: The Tax Accountant reviews the correction queue before each filing period. The goal is to reduce over-refunded `sr_return_tax` and recover unreconciled settlement amounts [ESTIMATE: depends on `sr_return_tax` and `sr_return_amt_inc_tax`]. Impact is measured as the corrected amount on reviewed lines versus a holdout sample.
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: sr_ticket_number, sr_item_sk, sr_store_sk, sr_return_amt, sr_return_tax, sr_return_amt_inc_tax, sr_fee, sr_refunded_cash, sr_reversed_charge, sr_store_credit, sr_return_quantity from store_returns; s_store_sk, s_store_name, s_tax_precentage from store. Approach: (1) JOIN store ON sr_store_sk = s_store_sk. (2) Engineer features: tax_rate_gap = sr_return_tax / NULLIF(sr_return_amt,0) - s_tax_precentage; inc_tax_gap = sr_return_amt_inc_tax - (sr_return_amt + sr_return_tax); settle_gap = (sr_refunded_cash + sr_reversed_charge + sr_store_credit) - sr_return_amt_inc_tax; fee_ratio = sr_fee / NULLIF(sr_return_amt,0); unit_amt = sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity. (3) Train an Isolation Forest per store with contamination=0.01 and n_estimators=200. (4) Output schema: sr_ticket_number, sr_item_sk, s_store_name, anomaly_score, tax_rate_gap, settle_gap, excess_tax_amount = GREATEST(tax_rate_gap,0)*sr_return_amt. (5) ai_query explains which component broke reconciliation and recommends a correction action, producing the refund correction queue sorted by excess_tax_amount.

use_cases.Name: Detect Refund Calculation Irregularities with Finance Reconciliation Queue
use_cases.Statement: Web refunds whose components do not reconcile can pay out more than the merchandise justifies, and no control currently catches them. Examples are a `wr_return_amt_inc_tax` that differs from `wr_return_amt` plus `wr_return_tax`, settlement splits across `wr_refunded_cash`, `wr_reversed_charge` and `wr_account_credit` that do not add up, or refund-per-unit above `i_current_price`.
use_cases.Solution: Databricks Genie Code engineers reconciliation residuals, implied tax-rate deviation by `wr_refunded_addr_sk`, and the ratio of refund-per-unit to list price. It trains an Isolation Forest on these multi-feature profiles to score every return for calculation irregularity. The final deliverable is a finance reconciliation queue ranked by anomaly score and overpaid amount.
use_cases.Business Value: The Finance Controller reviews the reconciliation queue before each refund close and claws back or corrects irregular settlements. This reduces overpaid refund value in `wr_return_amt_inc_tax` and prevents tax refund errors in `wr_return_tax` [ESTIMATE: depends on wr_return_amt_inc_tax].
use_cases.High Level Design: Using columns: wr_item_sk, wr_order_number, wr_refunded_addr_sk, wr_refunded_customer_sk, wr_return_quantity, wr_return_amt, wr_return_tax, wr_return_amt_inc_tax, wr_refunded_cash, wr_reversed_charge, wr_account_credit, wr_fee, wr_net_loss from web_returns; i_item_sk, i_current_price, i_wholesale_cost, i_category from item. Approach: JOIN item ON wr_item_sk = i_item_sk. Engineer these features: tax_identity_resid = wr_return_amt_inc_tax - (wr_return_amt + wr_return_tax); settle_resid = wr_return_amt_inc_tax - (wr_refunded_cash + wr_reversed_charge + wr_account_credit); implied_tax_rate = wr_return_tax / NULLIF(wr_return_amt,0); rate_dev = the absolute difference from the median implied_tax_rate of the same wr_refunded_addr_sk; unit_price_ratio = (wr_return_amt / NULLIF(wr_return_quantity,0)) / i_current_price; and loss_to_cost = wr_net_loss / NULLIF(i_wholesale_cost * wr_return_quantity,0). Standardize the features within i_category. Train an Isolation Forest (n_estimators=300, contamination=0.01). Output columns: wr_order_number, wr_item_sk, anomaly_score, the top contributing features (via SHAP) and estimated overpayment = MAX(settle_resid, unit refund above price). As the final step, ai_query writes a reconciliation note per flagged return with the suspected error type and the correction action.
